fermentables.name: Kiwi
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 1-23 EBC (typical 23) Kiwi, a tangy and tropical fruit known for its vibrant green color, has found an interesting application in the world of beer brewing. With a distinct flavor profile that combines sweet and tart notes with hints of citrus and tropical fruits, Kiwi is capable of elevating the taste of beer to new heights. Its unique characteristics influence the taste by adding a refreshing acidity and bright fruitiness that can complement or enhance other flavors present in the brew. In beer production, Kiwi is primarily used as an additive during fermentation or as a flavoring agent in specialty beers . Its properties work well with both lighter and darker styles, making it versatile for various brews. Kiwi 's high natural sugar content also aids in boosting alcohol levels during fermentation without compromising on flavor. Some popular beer styles brewed using Kiwi include wheat beers, pale ales, IPAs ( India Pale Ales ), sour beers, and even experimental fruity concoctions where brewers get creative with their recipes to deliver distinctive tasting experiences to consumers seeking something different from traditional offerings.

fermentables.name: Lactose (Milk Sugar)
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 0-1 EBC (typical 1) Lactose, also known as milk sugar, is a commonly used ingredient in beer brewing. It adds a distinct flavor profile to the finished product with its subtle sweetness and creamy texture. Lactose is unfermentable by yeast, meaning it remains in the final beer without being converted into alcohol during fermentation. This not only enhances the body and mouthfeel of the beer but also provides a smooth and velvety finish. Lactose contributes a mild sweetness that balances out bitterness from hops or roasted malts in certain styles of beer. It is often used to create sweeter and richer brews like milk stouts or cream ales . The addition of Lactose can give these beers an added complexity and depth while enhancing their overall drinkability. Aside from influencing taste, Lactose has unique properties that make it useful in brewing. Its unfermentable nature means it can be added at various stages of the brewing process without affecting primary fermentation or carbonation levels. Brewers typically add Lactose during boiling or post-fermentation to achieve desired sweetness levels.

fermentables.name: Lime
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 0-9 EBC (typical 4) Lime is a versatile fruit that finds its application in beer brewing, adding a unique flavor profile to the brew. It imparts a refreshing and tangy taste with citrus undertones, making it an excellent choice for those seeking a zesty twist to their beer. Lime influences the taste of beer by providing a bright acidity and enhancing the overall freshness of the beverage. In addition to its flavor contribution, Lime serves various purposes in beer brewing. It can be used during different stages of production, such as during mashing or fermentation, depending on the desired outcome. Lime also acts as a natural preservative due to its antibacterial properties and helps maintain stability within the brew. When it comes to specific beer styles brewed with Lime, popular choices include Mexican-style lagers like Corona or Pacifico, where Lime wedges are often added for an extra burst of citrus goodness. Additionally, some craft breweries experiment with incorporating Lime into wheat beers or sour ales for an interesting twist on traditional styles.

fermentables.name: Loganberry
fermentables.notes: Loganberry, a hybrid fruit that originated from a cross between blackberry and raspberry, has found its way into the world of beer brewing. Known for its rich and complex flavor profile, Loganberries bring a unique tartness and sweetness to brews. Its influence on the taste of beer is evident in the form of vibrant berry notes that complement various styles. In beer brewing, Loganberries are primarily used as an adjunct ingredient to enhance flavors rather than being fermented directly. This allows brewers to experiment with different combinations and create interesting flavor profiles. The properties of Loganberries lend themselves well to sour beers, fruit-infused IPAs, wheat beers, or even stouts when paired with chocolate undertones. The result is often a balanced blend where the natural acidity of the berries adds depth while harmonizing with other ingredients.

fermentables.name: Lychee
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 1-6 EBC (typical 4) Lychee, a tropical fruit native to Southeast Asia, has found its way into the realm of beer brewing and is making quite an impact. Known for its sweet and floral flavor profile with hints of rosewater and grape, Lychee adds a unique twist to traditional beer recipes. Its presence in the brewing process infuses the beverage with a distinct fruity aroma and taste that is both refreshing and tantalizing. When used in beer brewing, Lychee acts as an adjunct ingredient that enhances the overall flavor experience. It brings a delightful sweetness without being overpowering while also contributing subtle floral notes that complement various styles of beer. Brewers often use Lychee to create light-bodied beers such as wheat or pale ales, where its delicate flavors can shine through. Additionally, its properties lend themselves well to sour or fruited beers where it can contribute acidity and complexity.

fermentables.name: Maize
fermentables.notes: Also known as: Corn Beer Analytics subtype: Unmalted Adjunct Typical color range: 0-9 EBC (typical 3) Maize, also known as corn, is widely used in beer brewing due to its unique flavor profile and properties. It adds a subtle sweetness and smoothness to the taste of beer, making it a popular choice for brewers looking to create well-balanced and refreshing brews. Maize serves as an adjunct in the brewing process, meaning it is added alongside malted grains like barley or wheat. Maize contributes to a lighter body and color while enhancing drinkability by reducing bitterness. Its natural sugars are converted into alcohol during fermentation, resulting in a clean and crisp finish. Additionally, Maize helps improve head retention in beers by providing proteins that aid in foam formation. Maize finds application across various beer styles such as American lagers, cream ales, Mexican-style lagers (like Corona), and even some Belgian witbiers . These styles benefit from the inclusion of Maize as it imparts their characteristic lightness and easy-drinking nature.

fermentables.name: Malt Extract
fermentables.notes: Also known as: DME Typical color range: 4-79 EBC (typical 9) Malt Extract, available in dried (DME) or liquid (LME) form, has transformed the beer brewing process, making it accessible to more hobbyists. This is because the malt extract provides a convenient alternative to the traditional all-grain brewing method. Malt Extract is derived from malted grains, usually barley, where the sugars have been extracted and then either concentrated into a syrup (LME) or dehydrated into a powder (DME). This method eliminates the need for mashing, a time-consuming process used in all-grain brewing to extract fermentable sugars from malted grains. However, using malt extract over traditional grain malt can impact the final product. While malt extract can expedite the brewing process and often create a more consistent brew, all-grain brewing allows for greater control over the beer's flavor, color, and overall characteristics. Craft and professional brewers typically prefer the traditional grain malt method due to the increased scope for creativity and individuality it provides in beer creation. That said, malt extract brewing serves as a valuable entry point into the craft for newcomers, offering a less labor-intensive and less error-prone method while still producing quality beer.

fermentables.name: Maltodextrin
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 0-7 EBC (typical 6) Maltodextrin, a sugar derived from starch, is commonly used in beer brewing as a way to enhance body and mouthfeel. It has a neutral flavor profile, meaning it does not add any noticeable taste or aroma to the beer. Instead, Maltodextrin primarily influences the texture of the beer by increasing its viscosity and providing a fuller mouthfeel. In addition to improving body and mouthfeel, Maltodextrin serves various purposes in beer brewing. It can be used to increase the alcohol content without adding excessive sweetness or flavor. Maltodextrin also aids in head retention by providing proteins that stabilize foam formation. Furthermore, it acts as an adjunct ingredient that helps balance out bitter flavors in hop-forward beers. The properties of Maltodextrin make it highly suitable for use in different styles of beer. Its ability to boost body and improve mouthfeel makes it particularly popular in heavier styles such as stouts and porters where richness is desired. However, it can also be utilized in lighter styles like pale ales or lagers when brewers want to add substance without altering the overall character too much.

fermentables.name: Mango

Its unique taste is influencing the overall flavor of beers by adding a refreshing fruity sweetness and a hint of tropical notes. The addition of > Mango enhances the complexity and depth of flavors in beer, making it an ideal choice for those looking to experiment with different ingredients. Mango is mainly used as an adjunct ingredient in beer brewing. It can be added during various stages such as fermentation or conditioning to infuse its distinct taste into the final product. Mango 's properties contribute not only to the flavor but also to the aroma and color of the brew. With its high sugar content, > Mango provides fermentable sugars that are converted into alcohol during fermentation. Brewers often incorporate mango in lighter styles such as wheat beers, pale ales, IPAs ( India Pale Ales ), or even sour beers. These styles complement the natural sweetness and tropical character imparted by > Mango, resulting in a well-balanced and flavorful beverage that appeals to both fruit-loving enthusiasts and traditional beer drinkers alike.

fermentables.name: Maple Syrup
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 69-92 EBC (typical 92) Maple Syrup is a versatile ingredient that adds a unique flavor profile to beer brewing. It imparts a rich, sweet taste with hints of caramel and toffee, enhancing the complexity of the brew. The distinct flavors from the syrup can range from subtle undertones in lighter beers to more prominent notes in darker and heavier styles. Influencing both aroma and taste, Maple Syrup is primarily used as an adjunct or flavoring agent in beer production. Its natural sweetness helps balance out bitterness while adding depth and richness to the overall flavor profile. The properties of Maple Syrup also contribute to improved mouthfeel, giving the beer a smooth and velvety texture. Beer styles that are typically brewed with Maple Syrup include stouts, porters, brown ales, barleywines, and even some Belgian-style beers. These styles benefit from its robust sweetness and complement it well with their malty backbone. As a sugar source during fermentation or added post-fermentation for enhanced character, Maple Syrup brings an enticing twist to these already complex brews.

fermentables.name: Molasses
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 80-212 EBC (typical 212) Molasses, a thick and viscous byproduct of sugar production, is widely used in beer brewing due to its rich flavor profile. It imparts a distinct deep caramel and earthy taste that adds complexity to the overall flavor profile of the beer. The use of Molasses can greatly influence the taste of beer, giving it a sweet and robust character. Aside from its flavor contribution, Molasses also serves as a fermentable source of sugars for yeast during fermentation. This helps increase the alcohol content in the final product while adding depth to the body and mouthfeel. Its properties include being highly fermentable yet offering residual sweetness, contributing both color and aroma to the brew. Molasses finds application in various styles of beer such as stouts, porters, brown ales, and Belgian dubbels among others. These styles benefit from its bittersweet notes that complement roasted malts or add complexity alongside spices like cinnamon or nutmeg commonly found in winter warmers or holiday beers. With its unique flavor profile and versatile usage potential, Molasses continues to be an essential ingredient for brewers looking to craft bold and flavorful beers.

fermentables.name: Oat Malt
fermentables.notes: Also known as: Malted Oats Beer Analytics subtype: Other Malt Typical color range: 1-11 EBC (typical 4) Oat Malt is a versatile ingredient in beer brewing, offering a unique flavor profile and influencing the taste of the final product. It adds a smooth and creamy mouthfeel to beers, along with subtle nutty and biscuity flavors. This contributes to a fuller body and enhanced richness in the brew. This grain is primarily used for its properties as a malted grain rather than for its fermentable sugars. Oat Malt helps improve head retention, giving beers that desirable frothy foam on top. Additionally, it aids in enhancing stability by reducing haze formation due to proteins present in oats. Oat Malt finds its application across various beer styles, including stouts, porters, pale ales, and even IPAs . Its light color allows brewers flexibility when crafting different recipes while still achieving desired characteristics such as silkiness or creaminess without overpowering other ingredients or altering the appearance of the beer significantly. So whether you're seeking to create an oatmeal stout with rich chocolate notes or want to add depth to your hop-forward ale, incorporating Oat Malt into your brewing process can elevate both flavor and texture of your beverage.

fermentables.name: Orange
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 1-12 EBC (typical 7) Orange is a versatile fruit that lends its unique flavor profile to beer brewing. With its bright, citrusy aroma and sweet yet tangy taste, Orange adds a refreshing twist to the traditional beer recipes. The distinct flavor of Orange can greatly influence the overall taste of beer, enhancing it with zesty notes that complement various styles. In beer brewing, Oranges are primarily used for their zest or juice. The essential oils found in the peel bring out vibrant citrus flavors when added during different stages of fermentation or conditioning. Orange zest can infuse beers with hints of bitterness and acidity while also imparting a pleasant fragrance. Additionally, using Orange juice in certain beer styles can contribute natural sugars and acids that aid in fermentation. The properties of Oranges make them an ideal ingredient for numerous beer styles such as Belgian witbiers, pale ales, IPAs ( India Pale Ales ), and even sour beers like gose or Berliner weisse . Witbiers often feature pronounced Orange character due to the addition of both zest and sometimes juice during brewing processes. In hop-forward styles like IPAs, adding Orange peel can provide an extra layer of complexity to balance out the intense hoppiness.

fermentables.name: Pale Chocolate
fermentables.notes: Also known as: Chocolate Light Beer Analytics subtype: Roasted Typical color range: 400-961 EBC (typical 551) Pale Chocolate is a roasted grain that adds a unique flavor profile to beer brewing. Unlike traditional chocolate malt, Pale Chocolate has a lighter color and milder flavor. It imparts subtle hints of cocoa, coffee, and nuttiness to the beer, creating a smooth and balanced taste. This ingredient brings complexity and depth to the brew without overwhelming other flavors. When used in beer brewing, Pale Chocolate contributes rich notes of dark chocolate and roasted coffee while maintaining a delicate sweetness. It enhances the overall complexity of the beer's flavor profile by adding layers of depth and richness. Breweries often use Pale Chocolate in darker styles such as stouts, porters, brown ales, or Belgian dubbels where its mild roast character can complement or enhance the existing malt backbone. Properties-wise, Pale Chocolate is distinguished by its black color achieved through roasting at lower temperatures compared to regular chocolate malts. Its gentle roast allows for more control over the level of bitterness imparted on the finished product. With just enough toastiness and subtle sweetness from this grain type, brewers have flexibility in achieving desired flavors while avoiding excessive acridness or harshness sometimes associated with darker malts.

fermentables.name: Pale Wheat Malt
fermentables.notes: Also known as: White Wheat Malt Beer Analytics subtype: Base Malt Typical color range: 3-8 EBC (typical 4) Pale Wheat Malt is a crucial ingredient in beer brewing, known for its distinct flavor profile. It imparts a subtly sweet and bready taste to the beer, which complements other ingredients like hops and yeast. This malt greatly influences the overall taste of the beer by adding depth and complexity. Pale Wheat Malt is primarily used as a base malt in many beer recipes, providing fermentable sugars that contribute to alcohol content during fermentation. Its properties include being light in color, lending clarity to the final product while still maintaining some haze characteristic of wheat beers. Due to its unique qualities, Pale Wheat Malt is commonly used in traditional German-style hefeweizens and Belgian witbiers where it adds body and enhances head retention. Additionally, it can be utilized in American wheat beers or pale ales for added texture and flavor dimensionality.

fermentables.name: Papaya
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 0-1 EBC (typical 1) Papaya, a tropical fruit known for its vibrant color and sweet taste, is finding an interesting application in the world of beer brewing. When used as an ingredient in beer, papaya adds a unique flavor profile that often includes notes of tropical fruits such as mango and melon with hints of citrus. This infusion provides a refreshing and slightly tangy twist to traditional beer styles. The use of Papaya in beer greatly influences its taste by introducing fruity and exotic flavors that complement the maltiness or hoppiness typically associated with different types of beers. Whether it's a pale ale, IPA, or wheat beer, the addition of Papaya can enhance the overall flavor complexity and make each sip more enjoyable. Brewers utilize Papaya for various purposes beyond just adding flavor. It also contributes to enhancing the aroma and appearance of the final product. Papayas contain enzymes that aid fermentation, which can help brewers achieve desired characteristics like improved clarity or increased foam stability. Given its tropical nature, Papaya pairs exceptionally well with lighter beer styles such as pilsners or blonde ales where its flavors shine through without overpowering other ingredients. However, innovative brewers have experimented with incorporating this fruit into unconventional brews like sour beers or even stouts to create intriguing combinations that push boundaries within craft brewing.

fermentables.name: Peach
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 0-50 EBC (typical 12) Peach is a delicious fruit that brings a unique flavor profile to beer brewing. Known for its sweet and juicy taste, Peach adds a pleasant and refreshing dimension to the overall taste of the beer. It influences the beer by imparting fruity notes with hints of stone fruits and tropical flavors. When used in brewing, Peaches are typically added during fermentation or as an extract or puree during secondary fermentation. This allows the natural sugars from the fruit to ferment along with the other ingredients, resulting in a well-balanced brew with subtle Peach undertones. Peach is commonly utilized in various beer styles such as wheat beers, sour beers, pale ales, and even IPAs . Apart from its flavorful contribution, Peaches also bring certain properties to beer brewing. They contain natural enzymes that can aid in breaking down proteins during mashing, which can enhance clarity and improve mouthfeel. Additionally, Peaches are rich in antioxidants and vitamins that provide health benefits when consumed moderate amounts within beer.

fermentables.name: Pear

With its distinct flavor profile, Pear adds a crisp and slightly sweet taste to beers. It influences the taste by providing subtle fruity notes that complement various beer styles. Pear can be used in both traditional and experimental brews. Its properties make it an excellent addition for enhancing the overall complexity of different beer styles. It can be added during fermentation or as part of post-fermentation processes like dry hopping or blending with other fruits. The typical beer styles brewed with Pear range from light and refreshing options like wheat beers and saisons to more robust choices such as IPAs and stouts. The use of Pear helps create unique flavor combinations that appeal to craft beer enthusiasts seeking something new and exciting in their pint glass.

fermentables.name: Peated Malt
fermentables.notes: Also known as: Peated Malt Beer Analytics subtype: Base Malt Typical color range: 1-7 EBC (typical 5) Peated Malt, a type of base malt with a light color, is widely used in beer brewing due to its unique flavor profile. It imparts a distinct smoky and earthy taste, reminiscent of peat smoke found in whiskies from Scotland's Islay region. This characteristic flavor comes from the drying process during malting, where the grain is exposed to peat smoke. By incorporating Peated Malt into their recipes, brewers can significantly influence the taste of beer. The smoky notes brought by this ingredient add complexity and depth to both dark and lighter beer styles. Its flavors blend harmoniously with roasted malts or complement hop bitterness in pale ales or IPAs . Aside from enhancing flavor profiles, Peated Malt is also utilized for creating specific beer styles such as Scottish Ales and Scotch Ales . These brews often showcase rich caramel sweetness that intertwines seamlessly with the distinctive smokiness provided by Peated Malt . Whether used sparingly for subtle undertones or more heavily for an intense experience, this grain allows brewers to craft beers that are truly one-of-a-kind.

fermentables.name: Persimmon
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 8-52 EBC (typical 52) Persimmon, a delicious fruit known for its sweet and honey-like flavor, has found an interesting application in beer brewing. Its unique flavor profile adds a delightful twist to the taste of beer, resulting in a slightly fruity and aromatic brew. The inclusion of Persimmon can bring notes of tropical fruits, caramelized sugars, and even hints of vanilla or spice to the final product. In addition to enhancing the flavor experience, Persimmons are used in beer brewing primarily for their fermentable sugar content. These sugars provide food for yeast during fermentation, leading to increased alcohol production and contributing to the overall mouthfeel and body of the beer. Persimmons also contain enzymes that aid in breaking down starches into simpler sugars, which further aids in fermentation. The properties of Persimmon make it suitable for various beer styles like Belgian tripels or strong ales where higher alcohol content is desired. It can also be utilized in lighter styles such as wheat beers or saison-style brews to add complexity and balance out other ingredients. With its versatile nature and distinct flavors, Persimmon offers brewers an exciting ingredient option for creating unique and flavorful beers.

Its influence on the taste is characterized by subtle notes of biscuit, bread crusts, and honey-like sweetness. With its mild yet flavorful properties, Pilsner Light Malt is widely used as the primary ingredient in traditional pilsners and lagers. It provides a clean and refreshing quality to these styles while also lending a gentle malty backbone. Additionally, this malt can be utilized in other lighter beer styles such as golden ales or blonde ales to achieve similar characteristics.

It has a light color, making it ideal for producing pale lagers and pilsners. Pilsner Malt serves as the foundation of these beer styles, providing fermentable sugars and contributing to the overall flavor profile. The flavor profile of beers brewed with pilsner malt tends to be clean, crisp, and slightly sweet. It imparts a delicate grainy or biscuity taste that enhances the overall balance of the beer. Pilsner Malt also has a high enzymatic activity, which helps with the conversion of starches into fermentable sugars during mashing. fermentables.name: Pineapple
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 0-15 EBC (typical 1) Pineapple is a popular fruit that has found its way into the world of beer brewing, adding a unique and tropical flavor profile to certain brews. With its sweet and tangy taste, Pineapple brings a refreshing and exotic twist to traditional beers. Its influence on the taste of beer can range from subtle hints of citrus and tropical notes to bold bursts of fruity flavors. Pineapple can be used in various ways during the brewing process. It can be added directly as fresh or canned fruit during fermentation or as juice during secondary fermentation. Pineapple 's natural enzymes also make it useful for breaking down proteins, aiding in clarity and creating a smooth mouthfeel in some styles of beer. Due to its distinct properties and flavor characteristics, Pineapple is often used in lighter-bodied beers such as wheat beers, pale ales, IPAs ( India Pale Ales ), and even sour beers. These styles are well-suited for incorporating Pineapple because they allow the fruit's bright flavors to shine through without overpowering other elements within the beer itself. Whether enjoyed on hot summer days or as an unexpected twist year-round, Pineapple -infused brews offer drinkers an exciting departure from more traditional options.

fermentables.name: Planet - Pale Ale Malt
fermentables.notes: Planet has a high yield and performs very well in the brewhouse. We recommend a mashing temperature of at least 65°C as this is the average gelatinisation temperature for this variety. Mashing at a lower temperature could cause a slow conversion or even stall as the starch might not fully gelatinise. Planet has a cereal-forward taste complemented with a mild nuttiness, imparted because of its slightly higher attenuation level. It has a lower ‘masking’ effect than Venture or Maris Otter leading to an increase in the impact of aroma hops and yeast aromas. Care must be taken as this also means that any brewing errors are less easily covered. In our tests, Planet has performed very well and feedback from brewers using this variety has been very positive, particularly with extract levels and flavour profiles. This traditional pale malt is ideal for classic top fermented beers. Suitable for IPA’s, bitters, golden ales and light beers. Pale is slightly darker and “maltier” than lager malt, whilst the extra pale is similar in colour to lager malts but with pale malt qualities

fermentables.name: Plum
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 0-132 EBC (typical 5) Plum, a versatile fruit, has found its way into the world of beer brewing. With its distinctive sweet and tangy flavor profile, Plum adds a unique twist to traditional beer recipes. Its influence on the taste of beer is evident in the subtle fruity notes it imparts, enhancing the overall complexity of the brew. The application of Plum in beer brewing is primarily for flavor enhancement and experimentation. It can be used at different stages of the brewing process - from adding fresh Plums during fermentation to incorporating Plum extracts or purees during conditioning. Plum 's properties as a fruit bring an added depth and richness to beers, creating a pleasant balance between sweetness and acidity. Typical beer styles that are brewed with Plum include fruit-infused wheat beers such as Belgian Witbiers or German Berliner Weisses . The tartness of Plums pairs well with these lighter-bodied beers, providing a refreshing and slightly sour character. Additionally, some breweries experiment with using Plum in darker beer styles like stouts or porters to introduce hints of dark fruits alongside their roasted malt flavors for a more complex drinking experience.

fermentables.name: Pomegranate
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 1-278 EBC (typical 105) Pomegranate has become a popular ingredient in beer brewing due to its unique flavor profile. It adds a sweet and tangy taste with hints of tartness, making it an excellent addition for those looking to experiment with fruit flavors in their brews. The Pomegranate 's influence on the taste of beer is notable, as it can transform a regular beer into a refreshing and fruity beverage. The use of Pomegranate in beer brewing extends beyond just adding flavor. Its properties also contribute to the color and aroma of the final product. Pomegranate is often used as both a primary flavoring agent and as an adjunct during fermentation or aging stages. This versatile fruit pairs well with various styles such as wheat beers, sour beers, saisons, and even stouts.

fermentables.name: Prickly Pear
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 12-176 EBC (typical 23) Prickly Pear, a fruit native to the Americas, has found its way into the world of beer brewing. Known for its vibrant pink color and unique flavor profile, Prickly Pear adds a refreshing and slightly sweet taste to beers. Its influence on the taste of beer can range from subtle undertones to more pronounced fruity notes depending on how it is used in the brewing process. Prickly Pear is primarily used as an adjunct ingredient in beer brewing. It can be added during fermentation or incorporated into the mash to extract its flavors and colors. Additionally, it is often utilized alongside other fruits such as citrus or berries to create complex and well-balanced brews. Apart from enhancing flavor, Prickly Pear also brings some notable properties to beer brewing. The fruit contains high levels of antioxidants which can contribute to preserving freshness in beers over time. Furthermore, Prickly Pears are rich in essential vitamins and minerals that can add nutritional value to brewed beverages. While there are no specific styles exclusively brewed with Prickly Pear, it pairs exceptionally well with lighter-bodied beers such as wheat ales or lagers due to its delicate sweetness and aroma presence. These styles allow the flavors of Prickly Pear shine through without overpowering other elements present in the beer.

fermentables.name: Pronghorn – Brewski Pale
fermentables.notes: This malt was made from an exclusive two row barley developed by North Dakota State University designed with the brewer in mind. Two Track Malting was able be the first to commercially malt this and we are excited to be the only ones growing and malting this special barley. Arrow K Farms grew this barley in Belfield, ND and is in Pronghorn country where this malt got its name. Arrow K Farms is a seed farm and crops are grown with quality as a top priority.

fermentables.name: Prunes
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 1-252 EBC (typical 24) Prunes, the dried form of plums, have found a unique application in beer brewing. With their rich and sweet flavor profile, Prunes contribute to enhancing the taste of beer by adding notes of caramel, dark fruit, and subtle acidity. The addition of Prunes in the brewing process influences both the aroma and flavor profile of the beer, creating a complex yet balanced taste. Prunes are primarily used as an adjunct ingredient in brewing to impart specific characteristics to different styles of beers. Their properties include high sugar content that ferments into alcohol during fermentation, providing additional sweetness and body to the final product. Additionally, Prunes contain natural tannins that add depth and complexity to beers while contributing a slight dryness on the palate. The typical beer styles brewed with Prunes include strong ales such as Belgian quadrupels or barleywines. These styles benefit from the prune's ability to enhance maltiness while balancing it with its inherent fruity sweetness. Prune-infused beers often exhibit deep amber hues along with layers of flavors ranging from toasted maltiness to hints of ripe stone fruits like plum or raisin.

fermentables.name: Pumpkin
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 0-44 EBC (typical 33) Pumpkin is a versatile ingredient used in beer brewing, adding unique flavors and aromas to the final product. Its flavor profile can range from subtle earthiness to rich sweetness with hints of spice. When incorporated into beer recipes, pumpkin influences the taste by imparting a smooth and slightly sweet character that complements the malt and hops. In addition to its distinct flavor, pumpkin also contributes certain properties that enhance the overall quality of beer. It adds body and depth to the mouthfeel, resulting in a smoother texture. Pumpkin is often used for seasonal beers such as Oktoberfest or fall-themed brews like pumpkin ale or spiced pumpkin stout. Brewers utilize various techniques like roasting or pureeing pumpkins during different stages of brewing to extract maximum flavor. The result is an array of traditional styles brewed with pumpkin, including amber ales, porters, stouts, and even sour beers. These styles showcase the versatility of this fruit in creating deliciously complex beverages enjoyed by many craft beer enthusiasts during autumn months specifically but not limited to it given their increasing popularity throughout the year.

fermentables.name: Quince
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 1-20 EBC (typical 20) Quince, a versatile fruit known for its distinct flavor profile, has found its way into the world of beer brewing. With a unique combination of tartness and sweetness reminiscent of apples and pears, Quince adds an intriguing element to beer recipes. Its influence on the taste of beer can vary depending on how it is used - from subtle undertones that enhance other flavors to bold fruity notes that take center stage. The application of Quince in beer brewing serves multiple purposes. It can be used as a primary ingredient, contributing to both the aroma and taste profiles of the final product. Quince 's properties lend themselves well to creating balanced brews with complex layers of flavor. Additionally, Quince can be employed during fermentation or aging processes to impart specific characteristics such as acidity or additional sweetness. Various beer styles benefit from incorporating Quince into their recipes. These include sour beers like lambics or gueuzes where the sharpness and tanginess of Quince create harmonious complexity alongside wild yeast strains. Quinces are also commonly used in Belgian-style fruit beers, adding depth and richness to complement traditional malt flavors. The versatility and distinctive qualities make Quinces an exciting choice for brewers looking to push boundaries and experiment with new tastes in their creations

fermentables.name: Rahr High DP Distillers Malt

This product is extremely high in diastatic power and alpha amylase along with high levels of FAN for yeast nutrition.

fermentables.name: Rahr Kilned Caramel 30
fermentables.notes: Rahr Kilned Caramel malts give your beer color, aroma, flavor, and body, but without the prominent sweetness of drum-roasted caramel malts. Our Kilned Caramel 30 adds rich golden-red color and notes of bread, honey, and caramel.

fermentables.name: Rahr Kilned Caramel 47
fermentables.notes: Rahr Kilned Caramel malts give your beer color, aroma, flavor, and body, but without the prominent sweetness of drum-roasted caramel malts. Our Kilned Caramel 47 is named in honor of 1847, the year William Rahr founded our company. It imparts bronze-red color and nutty, grainy, and mild caramel notes.

fermentables.name: Rahr Kilned Caramel 80
fermentables.notes: Rahr Kilned Caramel malts give your beer color, aroma, flavor, and body, but without the prominent sweetness of drum-roasted caramel malts. Our Kilned Caramel 80 brings deep red-amber color along with nutty, caramel, bread crust, and grainy character.

fermentables.name: Rahr North Star Pils
fermentables.notes: A base malt to set your compass by! Rahr North Star Pils is crafted to meet the requirements of brewers looking for a domestic pilsner malt with low color and low modification. It is malted to a target of 38-40° Kolbach to facilitate smooth lautering with any mash regimen.

fermentables.name: Rahr Old World Pilsner
fermentables.notes: Rahr Old World Pilsner is special because it doesn't germinate as quickly as other domestic two-rows which means that more of the insoluble protein is left in the kernel. In this, the malt is giving up some extract but delivers greater flavor, yeast nutrients, and some beer foam stability in return. Also, this malt is lower in DP which means that when step-mashing some starch will convert in the higher temperature range.

fermentables.name: Rahr Pale Ale
fermentables.notes: Rahr Pale Ale is an ale-style base malt made from a blend of North American 2-row barleys. It has an excellent color, slightly darker than Rahr Standard or Pilsner malts, good malt flavor, and high extract yield. Well suited to American, English or continental ales, Rahr Pale Ale has become a popular base malt for almost any style of beer.

fermentables.name: Rahr Premium Pilsner
fermentables.notes: Rahr Premium Pilsner is an lager-style base malt made from premium North American 2-row barley. Its light color, neutral flavor, and low protein content make Premium Pilsner an excellent choice for brewing clear, clean-tasting lagers.

fermentables.name: Rahr Red Wheat
fermentables.notes: Rahr Red Wheat is a pale wheat malt made from North American hard spring red wheat. Pale wheat malt has the sweet malty flavor of other malted grains, but with a hint of fruitiness. Wheat malts are high in protein, which helps produce fuller-bodied beers. Wheat malt can improve head formation and retention, depending upon the other grist constituents. Red wheat has a slight tartness to its flavor not present in white wheat. It also has smaller, harder kernels than white wheat, which can require careful milling. Rahr Red Wheat is suitable for all wheat-style beers.

fermentables.name: Rahr Standard 2-Row
fermentables.notes: Rahr Standard 2-Row is a light-colored base malt made from a blend of North American 2-Row barley varieties. It is darker than most lager malts, but lighter than most pale ale malts. It has moderate protein levels, and good extract yield. Its neutral characteristics make it extremely versatile, and it is widely used by North American craft breweries as their standard base malt for any beer style.

fermentables.name: Rahr Standard 6-Row
fermentables.notes: Rahr Standard 6-Row is a light-colored base malt made from a blend of North American 6-Row barley varieties. 6-row barley has a much higher protein content and enzymatic power than 2-row barley. Inclusion of Standard 6-Row is therefore very advantageous for recipes calling for large proportions of specialty malts, wheat malts, or adjuncts, which have little or no enzymatic power themselves. 6-row barley is also used to match historical beer styles from settings where 2-row barley was not widely available. High proportions of 6-row barley may necessitate the use of adjuncts or require protein rests in mashing.

fermentables.name: Rahr Unmalted Wheat
fermentables.notes: Rahr Unmalted Wheat is a raw wheat grain. Unmalted Wheat has a strong grain flavor, and a very light straw color. It is used in many traditional Belgian styles to add flavor and cloudiness, and improve head formation. The starch in raw grain is not gelatinized and the protein content is high. Depending upon use, a cereal mash and/or protein rest may be required.

fermentables.name: Rahr White Wheat
fermentables.notes: Rahr White Wheat is a pale wheat malt made from North American soft winter white wheat. Pale wheat malt has the sweet malty flavor of other malted grains, but with a hint of fruitiness. Wheat malts are high in protein, which helps produce fuller-bodied beers. Wheat malt can improve head formation and retention, depending upon the other grist constituents. White wheat is easier to mill than red wheat, and more conducive to the haze characteristic of Belgian white beers. Rahr White Wheat is suitable for all wheat-style beers.

fermentables.name: Raisins
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 0-159 EBC (typical 12) Raisins, as a fruit, have found an interesting application in beer brewing. When used in the brewing process, they bring a unique flavor profile to the table. Raisins add notes of sweetness and subtle tartness to the beer, lending it a complex and fruity taste. The influence on the overall taste can vary depending on the amount of Raisins used and when they are added during fermentation. Typically, Raisins are utilized in brewing for their ability to enhance flavors or contribute to specific styles of beer. They can be added directly into the mash or boiled with other ingredients during wort production. Due to their high sugar content, Raisins provide fermentable sugars that yeast can convert into alcohol, contributing both flavor and increased alcohol content. The properties of Raisins make them suitable for several different types of beers. They work particularly well in darker beer styles such as stouts or porters where their rich sweetness complements roasted malt flavors superbly. Additionally, Belgian-style beers like Dubbels or Tripels benefit from the addition of Raisins as they add complexity and depth to these already flavorful brews.

fermentables.name: Raspberry
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 0-292 EBC (typical 12) Raspberry is a fruit that finds its application in beer brewing, adding unique flavors and characteristics to the final product. Known for its distinct sweet-tart flavor profile, Raspberries bring a vibrant and fruity taste to beers. Their influence on the taste of beer can range from subtle hints of Raspberry to bold and dominant flavors depending on the amount used during brewing. In beer brewing, Raspberries are primarily used as a flavoring ingredient or adjunct to enhance the overall taste experience. They provide natural sweetness and acidity, balancing out other ingredients like hops and malt. Raspberry 's properties also contribute to the coloration of beers, giving them an appealing reddish hue. This versatile fruit can be incorporated into various beer styles such as wheat beers, stouts, sours, or even experimental brews where brewers aim to create unique flavor combinations by blending Raspberry with different ingredients.

fermentables.name: Rhubarb

Its distinct taste adds a refreshing and slightly sour note to beers, enhancing their complexity. The addition of Rhubarb can influence the overall taste of beer by providing an additional layer of acidity that balances out sweetness or richness in certain styles. In brewing, Rhubarb is primarily used as an adjunct ingredient rather than a dominant one. It pairs well with various fruits such as strawberries and raspberries, making it ideal for fruit-infused beers or sour styles like Berliner Weisse or Gose . Rhubarb 's properties include high levels of malic acid which contribute to its sharpness and bright red color. Additionally, it contains antioxidants and vitamins that can add some nutritional value to beer.

fermentables.name: Rice Hulls
fermentables.notes: Also known as: Rice Husks Beer Analytics subtype: Unmalted Adjunct Typical color range: 0-1 EBC (typical 0) Rice hulls, known as a grain adjunct in beer brewing, have become increasingly popular among brewers for their unique properties and flavor profile. These light-colored unmalted grains provide a neutral taste to the final product. When used in brewing, rice hulls play an essential role in enhancing the mouthfeel of beers by providing better filtration during the lautering process. The addition of rice hulls improves the overall clarity and stability of beer due to their filtering capabilities. This makes them particularly useful when working with high-protein malts or ingredients that tend to create stuck mashes or slow run-offs. Moreover, they prevent compacting and allow for improved drainage during mashing and sparging processes. Typically used in lager-style beers like American Adjunct Lagers or Japanese Rice Lagers, rice hulls contribute to lighter-bodied brews with crisp finishes. They are also commonly employed when crafting gluten-free beers using alternative grains such as sorghum or corn grits instead of traditional malted barley. In these cases, rice hulls aid in maintaining proper mash consistency while ensuring efficient wort extraction without affecting the desired flavors of other ingredients present in the recipe.

fermentables.name: Rice Syrup
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 1-4 EBC (typical 1) Rice Syrup, a sugar derived from rice, has found its application in beer brewing due to its unique flavor profile and properties. It imparts a light and crisp sweetness to the beer, enhancing the overall taste and mouthfeel. The use of Rice Syrup in brewing can result in a drier finish and lighter body compared to other sugars like malt or corn syrup. Rice Syrup is primarily used as an adjunct ingredient by brewers for various purposes. It can serve as a fermentable sugar source during the brewing process, providing additional alcohol content without adding excess flavors or colors. Rice Syrup also aids in improving head retention and promoting a clean fermentation profile. Due to its light flavor characteristics, Rice Syrup is commonly employed in brewing styles where subtlety is key. It is often used in lagers such as American Light Lager and Japanese Rice Lager, contributing to their refreshing nature while maintaining balance with other ingredients.

With its distinct smoky aroma and hints of coffee and chocolate, this malt greatly influences the taste of beer by adding complexity and depth. This specialty malt is primarily used for enhancing flavors in darker beers such as stouts, porters, and dark lagers. Its properties contribute to improving mouthfeel by providing body and texture. fermentables.name: Roasted Rye Malt
fermentables.notes: Also known as: Chocolate Rye Beer Analytics subtype: Roasted Typical color range: 483-879 EBC (typical 639) Roasted Rye Malt is a grain that adds a unique and distinct flavor profile to beer. It imparts rich, dark flavors with hints of coffee, chocolate, and roasted nuts. This malt contributes to the overall complexity and depth of taste in brewing by providing a bold and slightly spicy character. The use of Roasted Rye Malt greatly influences the taste of beer by adding depth and complexity through its pronounced roasted notes. Its intense flavors can enhance stouts, porters, or even pale ales by giving them an added layer of richness. Additionally, it provides a smooth mouthfeel which helps balance out the bitterness from hops. This malt is primarily used for dark beers such as stouts, porters, black IPAs ( India Pale Ales ), or brown ales due to its deep color ranging from dark brown to black. The properties of Roasted Rye Malt include high fermentability and good diastatic power which aids in the conversion of starches into sugars during mashing.

Its influence on the taste of beer is significant as it adds complexity and depth to the brew, enhancing its overall character. This malt is primarily used for adding color and flavor to darker beer styles such as stouts, porters, and schwarzbiers . With its intense black hue, Roasted Spelt Malt helps achieve the desired darkness in these beers while contributing distinct roasted notes that balance out any sweetness. Additionally, its properties include providing body and mouthfeel to the brews it's added into.

fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Other Malt Typical color range: 4-25 EBC (typical 7) Rye Malt is a versatile grain that adds a distinct flavor profile to beer brewing. Its flavor is characterized by its spicy, earthy notes and subtle sweetness. When used in the brewing process, Rye Malt influences the taste of beer by imparting a unique complexity and depth. It can enhance the overall maltiness of the brew while adding a touch of spiciness that sets it apart from traditional barley-based beers. Rye Malt is commonly used in various beer styles such as Roggenbier, which is a German style rye beer known for its full-bodied mouthfeel and pronounced spice character. Additionally, it is often utilized in American Pale Ales (APAs) and India Pale Ales ( IPAs ) to add an extra layer of complexity to these hop-forward styles. The properties of Rye Malt contribute not only to the flavor but also affect other aspects such as head retention and body texture due to its high protein content.

fermentables.name: Small Spelt Malt
fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Other Malt Typical color range: 3-12 EBC (typical 7) Small Spelt Malt is a grain that offers a unique flavor profile to beer brewing. It imparts a delicate nutty and biscuity taste, along with subtle hints of honey and spice. Its distinct flavor adds depth and complexity to the overall taste of the beer, making it an intriguing ingredient for brewers looking to experiment with different flavors. This malt is primarily used for its ability to enhance the malty character in beers. It contributes a smooth mouthfeel and helps create a rich caramel-like sweetness without overpowering other ingredients. Small Spelt Malt also aids in head retention, resulting in visually appealing beers with frothy foam on top. Due to its light color, it can be utilized in various beer styles such as Belgian-style Ales, Saisons, Wheat Beers, or even experimental recipes where brewers want to add some uniqueness to their creations.

fermentables.name: Smoke Malt
fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Base Malt Typical color range: 4-23 EBC (typical 7) Smoke Malt, a type of base malt with a light color, is widely used in beer brewing for its unique flavor profile and the distinct taste it imparts to the final product. The smoke malt brings smoky and sometimes earthy flavors reminiscent of smoked meats or campfires. These flavors provide an additional layer of complexity to the beer, giving it a rich and robust character that can be enjoyed by enthusiasts seeking something beyond traditional brews. The influence of Smoke Malt on the taste of beer is undeniable as it adds depth and enhances overall flavor profiles. It infuses notes such as bacon, peat, or even charred wood into beers. This makes it particularly popular in styles where these flavors are desirable or complementary, like rauchbier (a German style known for its intense smokiness) or certain stouts and porters. In addition to enhancing flavor, Smoke Malt also contributes to mouthfeel and body due to its grain properties. Smoke Malt finds itself predominantly utilized for crafting specialty beers that aim at delivering bold smoky undertones alongside other desired characteristics. Its distinctive properties make it an excellent choice when brewers wish to experiment with unique flavors while staying true to their craft's traditions. By skillfully incorporating this exceptional ingredient into various recipes, brewers can create memorable experiences for those seeking unconventional tastes in their favorite pint.

fermentables.name: Sorghum Syrup
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 1-52 EBC (typical 3) Sorghum syrup is a natural sweetener that has been used in beer brewing for centuries. It boasts a unique flavor profile, with hints of molasses, caramel, and honey-like sweetness. When added to beer recipes, it imparts a distinct taste that can range from subtle to pronounced depending on the amount used. The addition of Sorghum syrup influences the taste of beer by providing depth and complexity to its flavor profile. Its rich sweetness balances out bitterness and adds a pleasant touch of sweetness without overwhelming other flavors. This makes it an excellent choice for brewers looking to create well-rounded beers with a hint of sweetness. Sorghum syrup serves various purposes in brewing. It is commonly employed as an alternative source of fermentable sugars for gluten-free or gluten-reduced beers since it does not contain gluten like barley malt does. Additionally, Sorghum syrup can be utilized as a flavor enhancer or adjunct ingredient in traditional beers to augment their overall taste experience. It has high fermentability which allows yeast to easily convert its sugars into alcohol during fermentation. It also contributes color and body to the finished beer due to its natural viscosity and dark hue. Typical beer styles brewed with Sorghum syrup include gluten-free lagers and pale ales specifically designed for individuals with celiac disease or those seeking alternatives to traditional barley-based brews. These styles showcase the ability of Sorghum syrup to mimic some characteristics found in conventional malts while maintaining their own distinct flavors derived from this unique sugar source.

It imparts a nutty and slightly sweet taste to the beer, adding depth and complexity to the overall flavor profile. The use of Spelt Malt in brewing greatly influences the taste of beer by providing a distinct character that sets it apart from traditional barley malts. Apart from enhancing flavors, Spelt Malt also contributes additional properties to beers. It provides added body and mouthfeel while improving head retention, resulting in a fuller and creamier texture. Additionally, Spelt Malt adds subtle aromas reminiscent of bread or biscuits. Typically utilized in Belgian-style beers such as Saisons or Witbiers, Spelt Malt can be incorporated into various styles where brewers aim to create a more rustic or farmhouse character. fermentables.name: Stout Malt
fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Base Malt Typical color range: 1-9 EBC (typical 4) Stout Malt, a light-colored base malt used in beer brewing, adds distinct flavors and properties that greatly influence the taste of beer. Its flavor profile is characterized by subtle notes of roasted coffee, chocolate, and caramel. This lends a rich and malty sweetness to the brew, enhancing its complexity. Stout Malt is commonly utilized in darker beer styles such as stouts and porters due to its ability to impart deep color and robust flavors. Apart from contributing unique tastes, Stout Malt also possesses specific properties that make it well-suited for certain brewing applications. With its enzymatic power and high diastatic potential, this grain efficiently converts starches into fermentable sugars during mashing. Additionally, it offers excellent extract yield which contributes to higher alcohol content in the finished product. Given these attributes along with its appealing flavor profile, Stout Malt serves as an essential ingredient in crafting flavorful beers like Irish dry stouts or classic American porters .

fermentables.name: Strawberry
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 1-39 EBC (typical 12) Strawberries have a sweet and tangy flavor profile, which adds a delightful fruity twist to beer. When used in brewing, Strawberries can influence the taste of beer by imparting a refreshing and slightly tart character. The natural sweetness of Strawberries helps balance the bitterness of hops, creating a harmonious blend of flavors. Strawberry is primarily used as an adjunct ingredient or fruit addition during fermentation. Brewers often add fresh or frozen Strawberries directly into the fermenter to infuse their flavors into the brew. Additionally, Strawberry extracts or purees can also be utilized for more controlled and consistent results. Properties such as aroma, color, and acidity make Strawberries suitable for various beer styles. Strawberry -infused beers are commonly found in fruit beers like wheat ales or blonde ales where their light body allows the delicate Strawberry flavors to shine through without overpowering other ingredients. It's worth noting that while Strawberries do not provide significant fermentable sugars themselves due to low sugar content compared to some other fruits, they still contribute unique characteristics that elevate the overall drinking experience for beer enthusiasts looking for something different and delicious.

fermentables.name: Super Pale Ale Malt
fermentables.notes: The light colour and clean flavour profile of Super Pale Ale Malt lend themselves to multiple beer styles. Using this exceptional malt, brewers can create extremely low colour beer with reddish and copper hues, a characteristic which also lends itself to the creation of vibrantly coloured fruit-beers. Here, the low colour of the malt allows the colour of the selected fruit of choice to really shine through. Super Pale Ale Malt is our lightest pale malt, and is ideally suited for IPA, bitter, golden ales, and light beers.

fermentables.name: Super Vienna
fermentables.notes: Originally a custom malt project, our Super Vienna is the product of pushing the upper limits on a traditional Vienna malt . By increasing the color target of the final kiln step, we are able to create a darker Vienna malt that maintains enzymatic power, allowing it to be used up to 100% in a grist. This malt is outstanding in Octoberfests or other dark lagers and allows for a dryer finish without unfermentable sugars from caramel malts.

fermentables.name: Tangerine
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 2-20 EBC (typical 12) Tangerine, with its vibrant and tangy flavor profile, brings a refreshing twist to beer brewing. Its citrusy characteristics contribute to the overall taste of the beer by adding bright notes of sweetness and acidity. Tangerine is commonly used in brewing to enhance fruity flavors or bring a zesty kick to certain beer styles. The properties of Tangerine make it an excellent ingredient for creating unique brews. It contains high levels of natural sugars and acids that can complement different malt profiles in beers. The fruit's juice or zest is often added during various stages of fermentation or conditioning, allowing brewers to experiment with the intensity of Tangerine flavor desired. Tangerine finds its place in a plethora of beer styles, including pale ales, wheat beers, IPAs ( India Pale Ales ), and even sour beers. Its addition creates delightful combinations such as hoppy citrus-forward IPAs or crisp wheat beers with hints of Tangerine zest. Regardless of the style brewed, incorporating Tangerines into the process adds an invigorating twist that tantalizes the taste buds without overpowering other flavors present in the beer.

fermentables.name: Terroir Paulista Biscoito / Melanoidina
fermentables.notes: The biscuit malt is a special well modified malt and in the same way that the caramel goes through a "stewing" process at low temperatures for the action of proteases and production of the precursors of the "toasted bread" flavor. This malt is longer to cure at higher temperatures for the development of intense color and flavor. Due to the fact that it is subjected to high temperatures with high humidity, the enzymatic loss is considerable and, therefore, it must be used in mixture with base malts.

fermentables.name: Terroir Paulista Caramelo 1
fermentables.notes: Caramel malt is a special well-modified malt where, at the beginning of drying, it is "stuffed" for gelatinization and saccharification of starch and a higher curing temperature for caramelization of sugars. Due to the fact that it is subjected to high temperatures with high humidity, the enzymatic loss is considerable and, therefore, it must be used in mixture with base malts.

fermentables.name: Terroir Paulista Caramelo 130 EBC
fermentables.notes: Darker caramelized malt. Provides a strong sweet taste of caramel and baked bread, as well as a darker golden color to your beer. It is a malt that goes through the "stuffing" process to produce sugars and caramelize causing vitrification of part of the starch, which contributes to providing more body to the beer like other caramel malts, and also good production and retention of foam.

fermentables.name: Terroir Paulista Caramelo 2
fermentables.notes: Caramel 2 malt is a special well-modified malt and in the same way that caramel goes through a “stuffing” process at higher temperatures for the action of amylases and the production of precursors of the “caramel” flavor. This malt is longer to cure at higher temperatures for the development of intense color and flavor. Due to the fact that it is subjected to high temperatures with high humidity, the enzymatic loss is considerable and, therefore, it must be used in mixture with base malts.

fermentables.name: Terroir Paulista Caramelo 3
fermentables.notes: Caramel 3 malt is a special well-modified malt and in the same way that caramel goes through a "stuffing" process at higher temperatures for the action of amylases and the production of precursors of "caramel" flavor. Curing of this malt is longer at higher temperatures for the development of the desired intense color and flavor. Due to the fact that it is subjected to high temperatures with high humidity, the enzymatic loss is considerable and, therefore, it must be used in mixture with base malts.

fermentables.name: Terroir Paulista Carapálida
fermentables.notes: Caramel malt is a special well-modified malt where, at the beginning of drying, it is "stuffed" for gelatinization and saccharification of starch and formation of dextrins, responsible for the increase in the body of the beer. The curing temperature, different from the other caramels, is not very high which causes a very mild caramelization, but a strong sweet flavor. Due to the fact that it is subjected to high humidity temperatures, the enzymatic loss is considerable and, therefore, it must be used in mixture with base malts.

fermentables.name: Terroir Paulista IAC-600 Black Rice Malt
fermentables.notes: Black rice malt is a novelty at Atelier do Malte, which, in partnership with the producers of Alto do Marins, has been developing rice malt options to supply microbrewers and homemade brewers with gluten-free malt options and other national products for whom has creativity and likes news. The rice has the highest gelatinization temperature, and a test of the best brewing ramp is recommended to obtain a good enzymatic power and greater extract. Rice has extract and enzymatic power slightly below traditional barley, behaving like a caramelized malt in this regard .

fermentables.name: Terroir Paulista Munich
fermentables.notes: Munich malt is a special, well-modified malt that undergoes a short “stuffing” process at low temperature for the action of proteases and the production of precursors to the flavor of “toasted bread”. Drying is done at low temperatures and during curing it is subjected to high temperatures to gain color. There is a loss of mild enzymatic power due to high curing temperatures and should therefore be used in mixture with base malts.

fermentables.name: Terroir Paulista Pale Ale
fermentables.notes: Generally used as a base malt or in combination with other types of malt, Pale Ale is considered a special malt because it is more modified, that is, because it presents a greater degree of degradation of b-Glucans and greater production of enzymes, providing a more pronounced flavor and color than that of Pilsen malt. The curing time and temperature are not extreme, which allows the enzymes to support the use of special non-enzymatic malts such as caramel or roasted.

fermentables.name: Terroir Paulista Pilsen
fermentables.notes: It is considered a base malt because it has an excellent enzymatic power and that even together with portions of other malts of lower enzymatic power (caramels and / or roasted) it is able to “digest” all the starch in smaller sugars providing an excellent amount of simple sugars for yeast , that is, extract. For the maintenance of a light color and with a high level of enzymes, pilsen malt does not force its modification and must be taken care during drying so that the curing temperature is sufficient for elimination of DMS precursors and inactivation of oxidative enzymes and development of flavor without, however, compromising the proteolytic and amylolytic enzymes needed in brazing.

fermentables.name: Terroir Paulista Vienna
fermentables.notes: It is considered a special dark malt but can be used as a base malt or in combination with other types of malt, Vienna is a well-modified malt, and has enough enzymes for use in high percentages in the recipe. The curing time and temperature are not extreme, just above Pale Ale malt. Its degree of modification and more intense roasting provides intense flavor and color to the beer .

fermentables.name: Toasted Malt

fermentables.name: Toffee Malt
fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Toasted Typical color range: 10-27 EBC (typical 13) Toffee Malt, a toasted grain with a golden color, is widely used in beer brewing for its distinctive flavor profile. It imparts rich toffee-like flavors and aromas to the beer, adding depth and complexity to the taste. The malt's influence on the overall flavor of the brew can range from subtle hints of caramel sweetness to more pronounced notes reminiscent of buttery toffee. Besides enhancing the taste of beer, Toffee Malt serves various purposes in brewing. Its high enzyme content aids in converting starches into fermentable sugars during mashing, contributing to improved fermentation efficiency and higher alcohol content. Additionally, it provides body and mouthfeel while also increasing foam stability due to its protein content. Typically utilized in darker styles such as stouts, porters, brown ales, or even barleywines; Toffee Malt adds a delightful touch of sweetness and warmth that complements these robust beers exceptionally well. However, it can also be employed judiciously in lighter styles like pale ales or lagers for an added layer of complexity without overwhelming their delicate profiles.

fermentables.name: Toffee Malt

fermentables.name: Torrefied Wheat
fermentables.notes: Adding torrefied wheat to a brew at 2-5% is a well known and reliable way of adding a complex protein matrix to your beer whilst maintaining stable head formation and retention. With the rise of the NEIPA, hazy and smooth beer is becoming more popular. We thought it would be really interesting to try out our torrefied wheat in a NEIPA and it worked really well. At an inclusion of 15- 20% we achieved a stable haze and a solid mouthfeel that pair perfectly with a citrussy hop addition.

fermentables.name: Torrified Barley Malt
fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Unmalted Adjunct Torrified Barley Malt is a grain commonly used in beer brewing that adds unique flavors and characteristics to the final product. It has a light color and imparts a distinct malty flavor profile, with notes of toasted bread and biscuit. This malt plays a significant role in influencing the taste of beer by adding depth, complexity, and sweetness. Torrified Barley Malt is primarily employed as an adjunct in brewing. It aids in enhancing body and improving head retention while providing fermentable sugars for yeast to convert into alcohol during fermentation. Its properties allow it to easily absorb water without requiring mashing or steeping like traditional malted grains. Typical beer styles brewed using Torrified Barley Malt include English-style ales such as bitters, milds, stouts, and porters. These beers benefit from the added layers of caramel-like flavors contributed by this particular type of unmalted adjunct grain.

fermentables.name: Torrified Oats
fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Unmalted Adjunct Typical color range: 0-7 EBC (typical 7) Torrified Oats, a type of unmalted adjunct grain in brewing, brings unique flavors and properties to beer. It contributes a mild, nutty flavor profile that adds depth and complexity to the brew. The torrefaction process enhances the oats' natural sweetness while maintaining their light color. By incorporating Torrified Oats into beer recipes, brewers can achieve various taste enhancements. This ingredient imparts a smooth and creamy mouthfeel due to its high protein content. It also improves head retention, resulting in a luscious foam on top of the beer. Additionally, Torrified Oats adds body and helps balance out bitterness or acidity in certain styles. Primarily used as an adjunct grain, Torrified Oats serve multiple purposes in brewing processes. They aid in enhancing mouthfeel and creating silky textures often found in stouts, porters, or hazy IPAs . These oats are particularly useful when aiming for beers with more body without increasing maltiness or sweetness significantly.

fermentables.name: Torrified Wheat Malt
fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Unmalted Adjunct Typical color range: 1-4 EBC (typical 4) Torrified Wheat Malt is a grain used in beer brewing that adds unique flavors and properties to the final product. It has a distinct flavor profile characterized by biscuity, nutty, and toasted notes. When added to beer recipes, it imparts these flavors into the brew, contributing to its overall taste. Aside from influencing the flavor of beer, Torrified Wheat Malt also enhances its mouthfeel and head retention. This makes it an excellent addition for improving body and texture in various styles of beers. Breweries often use Torrified Wheat Malt in their recipes for light-bodied beers such as pale ales, wheat beers, hefeweizens or Belgian witbiers due to its light color.

fermentables.name: Triticale Malt
fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Other Malt Typical color range: 3-15 EBC (typical 7) Triticale Malt, a type of other malt with a light color, is gaining popularity in the beer brewing industry for its unique flavor profile and properties. It adds a distinct nutty and slightly spicy taste to beers, influencing their overall flavor. The use of Triticale Malt can enhance the complexity and depth of various beer styles by providing a subtle sweetness and earthy undertones. This versatile grain is typically used as an adjunct or specialty malt in brewing. Its high protein content contributes to improved head retention and body in the final product. Breweries often incorporate Triticale Malt in recipes for pale ales, IPAs, stouts, and even Belgian-style farmhouse saisons to add character and dimension to these beer styles. With its ability to impart both malty sweetness and interesting flavors, Triticale Malt offers brewers an exciting ingredient option that elevates their creations beyond traditional barley-based brews.

fermentables.name: Turbinado
fermentables.notes: Typical color range: 20-25 EBC (typical 25) Turbinado, a type of sugar commonly used in beer brewing, brings its distinct flavor profile and influences the taste of the final product. With its rich caramel-like flavor and subtle molasses undertones, Turbinado adds depth and complexity to beers. Its unique sweetness complements various styles by providing a smooth mouthfeel and enhancing overall balance. Apart from imparting flavors, Turbinado is primarily used as a fermentable sugar during the brewing process. It serves as an additional food source for yeast during fermentation, resulting in increased alcohol content without adding excessive sweetness or heaviness to the finished beer. Due to its high solubility rate, it easily dissolves into wort while also contributing desirable color characteristics. The properties of Turbinado make it suitable for different beer styles such as stouts, porters, Belgian ales, brown ales, and even some IPAs . Its ability to lend complexity without overpowering other ingredients allows brewers to create well-rounded brews with added depth. Whether highlighting roasted malts in dark beers or complementing fruity esters in Belgian-style ales – Turbinado has become an essential ingredient for craft brewers seeking unique flavor profiles in their creations.
