fermentables.name: Unmalted Barley
fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Unmalted Adjunct Typical color range: 2-247 EBC (typical 3) Unmalted Barley is a grain that brings a distinct flavor profile to beer brewing. It tends to impart a slightly sweet and nutty taste, with hints of breadiness and cereal grains. This unique flavor can add complexity and depth to the overall taste of the beer, making it an interesting ingredient for brewers seeking different nuances in their creations. In addition to its flavor contribution, Unmalted Barley also affects other properties of the beer. Its high protein content enhances head retention, resulting in a fuller and more persistent foam on top. Moreover, this adjunct helps improve body and mouthfeel by adding viscosity without excessive sweetness or heaviness. Brewers commonly use Unmalted Barley as part of their grist bill when crafting certain styles of beers such as Irish stouts or Belgian witbiers . In these recipes, it plays a crucial role in achieving specific characteristics like smoothness, creaminess, or haze formation respectively.

fermentables.name: Unmalted Buckwheat
fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Unmalted Adjunct Typical color range: 4-25 EBC (typical 11) Unmalted Buckwheat is a unique grain used in beer brewing. It adds a distinct flavor profile to the finished product, characterized by nutty and earthy notes with hints of honey and caramel. This ingredient significantly influences the taste of beer, imparting complexity and depth to the brew. In addition to its flavor contribution, Unmalted Buckwheat also serves various purposes in brewing. It enhances head retention and can add body and mouthfeel to the beer due to its high protein content. Furthermore, it aids in improving foam stability during pouring. Typically used as an adjunct grain, Unmalted Buckwheat brings additional properties such as increased haze formation and improved color stability. Its golden hue adds visual appeal to beers brewed with this ingredient. This versatile grain finds application in a range of beer styles including Belgian-style Saisons, Blonde Ales, or even experimental recipes where brewers seek innovative flavors and textures for their creations. Whether aiming for traditional or unconventional brews, incorporating Unmalted Buckwheat into beer recipes offers endless possibilities for creative experimentation within the craft brewing industry.

fermentables.name: Unmalted Emmer
fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Unmalted Adjunct Unmalted Emmer, a light-colored grain and an unmalted adjunct, has found significant application in beer brewing. Its flavor profile is characterized by nutty and earthy notes, adding depth to the taste of beer. This unique ingredient influences the overall flavor of the brew by contributing a robust and distinct character. The use of Unmalted Emmer in brewing serves multiple purposes. It enhances mouthfeel, promoting a smooth and creamy texture in the final product. Additionally, it aids in head retention, resulting in a more visually appealing beer with a frothy foam. Due to its properties as an adjunct grain, Unmalted Emmer acts as a natural source of fermentable sugars during the brewing process. Typically used alongside malted grains like barley or wheat, Unmalted Emmer can be employed across various beer styles including traditional German beers such as Hefeweizen or Dunkelweizen. Its addition adds complexity to these styles while maintaining their classic characteristics.

fermentables.name: Unmalted Millet
fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Unmalted Adjunct Typical color range: 1-710 EBC (typical 7) Unmalted Millet, a type of grain used as an unmalted adjunct in beer brewing, offers unique flavor characteristics that can greatly influence the taste of beer. It imparts a delicate and slightly sweet flavor profile with hints of grassy notes. This adds a subtle complexity to the overall taste experience. Due to its light color, Unmalted Millet is often incorporated into lighter beer styles such as lagers and pilsners. Its use helps enhance mouthfeel and head retention while contributing minimal impact on color or body. Brewers also utilize Unmalted Millet for gluten-free brewing purposes since it does not contain any gluten proteins found in traditional malted grains like barley or wheat. With its properties as an unmalted adjunct, Unmalted Millet serves multiple purposes in beer production. It aids in improving fermentation efficiency by providing additional fermentable sugars without adding excessive starches that could negatively affect clarity or stability. Additionally, it can contribute to better foam formation due to its high protein content, resulting in richer and longer-lasting heads on poured beers.

fermentables.name: Unmalted Oat
fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Unmalted Adjunct Typical color range: 1-6 EBC (typical 5) Unmalted Oat, a type of grain used in beer brewing, brings its distinct flavor profile and unique properties to the brewing process. It imparts a smooth and creamy mouthfeel with subtle nutty undertones to the finished beer. This adds complexity to the overall taste experience and enhances the body of the brew. The use of Unmalted Oat influences the taste of beer by contributing a silky texture and enhancing its creaminess. It also helps improve head retention, resulting in a visually appealing pint with a rich foam cap that lingers longer. Additionally, it provides additional proteins for yeast nutrition during fermentation. Brewers often utilize Unmalted Oat for its specific characteristics in various styles such as oatmeal stouts, New England IPAs (NEIPAs), or Belgian witbiers . Its light color allows brewers more flexibility when designing their recipes while still benefiting from its desired attributes without significantly impacting the final hue of their beers.

fermentables.name: Unmalted Rye
fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Unmalted Adjunct Typical color range: 3-8 EBC (typical 7) Unmalted Rye is a popular adjunct used in beer brewing, known for its unique flavor profile. It imparts a distinct spiciness and earthy character to the beer, making it an excellent choice for brewers looking to add complexity to their brews. The presence of Unmalted Rye can greatly influence the taste of beer by providing a subtle sweetness and contributing to a fuller body. Additionally, its spicy notes often complement hop bitterness or enhance other malt flavors. Aside from enhancing flavor, Unmalted Rye also contributes desirable properties to the brewing process. Its high protein content aids in improving head retention and mouthfeel in the final product. This grain is commonly used as an adjunct in various beer styles such as Belgian saisons, farmhouse ales, and some American-style IPAs . These styles benefit from Unmalted Rye 's ability to create a dry, crisp finish while adding depth and balance without overwhelming other ingredients present in the recipe.

fermentables.name: Unmalted Spelt
fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Unmalted Adjunct Typical color range: 3-33 EBC (typical 4) Unmalted Spelt, a light-colored grain used as an unmalted adjunct in beer brewing, brings unique flavor profiles to the final product. With its nutty and slightly sweet taste, Unmalted Spelt adds depth and complexity to beers. Its influence on the taste can range from subtle to prominent depending on the quantity used. As an adjunct ingredient is primarily used for enhancing mouthfeel and improving head retention in beers. Its high protein content contributes to a fuller body and increased foam stability. Additionally, Unmalted Spelt provides fermentable sugars that can be converted by enzymes present during mashing. Typical beer styles brewed with Unmalted Spelt include wheat beers, saisons, farmhouse ales, and Belgian-style brews. These styles benefit from the grain's ability to create a smooth texture while imparting distinct flavors that enhance their overall character. Whether it is contributing a delicate sweetness or adding earthy undertones, Unmalted Spelt plays an essential role in creating exceptional craft beers across various styles.

fermentables.name: Unmalted Triticale
fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Unmalted Adjunct Typical color range: 5-13 EBC (typical 13) Unmalted Triticale is a versatile grain that has gained popularity in beer brewing for its unique flavor profile and impact on taste. With a combination of wheat and rye characteristics, it brings a subtle earthiness and nuttiness to the beer, adding complexity to the overall flavor. The use of Unmalted Triticale in brewing influences the taste by providing a slightly spicy note along with hints of caramel and bread-like flavors. In beer brewing, Unmalted Triticale is primarily used as an adjunct grain. It contributes to the body, mouthfeel, and head retention of the beer while enhancing its aroma and flavor without overpowering other ingredients. Its properties make it particularly suitable for Belgian-style beers such as saisons or farmhouse ales where it complements fruity esters produced by yeast fermentation. Additionally, Unmalted Triticale can be utilized in experimental brews or mixed with malted grains to create unique recipes that showcase its distinctive attributes.

fermentables.name: Unmalted Wheat
fermentables.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Unmalted Adjunct Typical color range: 1-12 EBC (typical 4) Unmalted Wheat is a popular ingredient used in beer brewing due to its unique flavor profile. It adds a distinct crispness and lightness to the overall taste of the beer, making it an excellent choice for refreshing summer brews or lighter beer styles. Its influence on the taste of beer can range from providing a subtle grainy sweetness to enhancing the mouthfeel by adding body and foam stability. In addition to influencing the flavor, Unmalted Wheat also has several desirable properties that make it valuable in brewing. Its high protein content contributes to improved head retention and haze formation, while its low starch content helps prevent excessive cloudiness in the finished product. This makes it particularly suitable for traditional wheat beers like Hefeweizens and Witbiers, as well as American wheat beers .

fermentables.name: Vienna Malt

It acts as the backbone of many classic lagers, such as Vienna Lager and Märzen, contributing to their balanced flavor profiles. Vienna Malt has moderate enzymatic activity and good fermentability. Its kilning process gives it a unique balance between color development and enzyme preservation. This makes it ideal for both single infusion mashes and decoction mashes, allowing brewers flexibility in their brewing techniques. It is valued for its versatility and ability to enhance the flavor of various beer styles. Its distinctive characteristics make it an essential ingredient in creating beers with depth, complexity, and balanced sweetness.

It imparts rich notes of caramel, toffee, and toasted grains which contribute to a malty sweetness while also providing a subtle smoky aroma. The use of Whisky Malt in beer brewing is predominantly for enhancing the overall flavor profile. Its properties lend a smooth mouthfeel along with an added layer of complexity that elevates the brew's taste experience. fermentables.name: White Rice Malt TERROIR PAULISTA
fermentables.notes: WHITE RICE MALT is a novelty from Atelier Do Malte. We have been developing malt options to supply microbrewers and home-made adventurers with new options of GLUTEN-FREE MALT and different NATIONAL products for those with creativity and looking for novelties. A disadvantage of working with uncooked rice as an adjunct to beer is its high gelatinization temperature, making it difficult to break down starch in sugars, generating a low extract, and also the lack of enzymes to guarantee the breakdown of numerous substances in rice and needing a separate decoction process. However, we offer you RICE MALT. During the malting process, several substances break down, such as proteins, beta glucans and polysaccharides, as well as the production and release of enzymes that will break these substances evenly during mashing. For this reason, RICE MALT has a lower gelatinization temperature and has enzymes that will assist in the production of a must suitable for the growth of yeast and the production of your beer, which can be called gluten-free beer.

fermentables.name: Youngberry
fermentables.notes: Youngberry, a delicious fruit known for its sweet and tart flavor profile, has found an intriguing application in the world of beer brewing. Its unique taste brings a refreshing twist to traditional beer recipes, making it a popular choice among brewers looking to experiment with new flavors. When added to the brewing process, Youngberry infuses the beer with hints of berry sweetness and acidity, providing a vibrant burst of flavor that complements various types of beers. The influence of Youngberry on the taste of beer is remarkable. It adds fruity notes that enhance the overall drinking experience and create a more complex profile. This ingredient can be used in both ale and lager styles, offering flexibility to brewers seeking to craft different variations. Additionally, Youngberry 's properties contribute not only its distinct taste but also its vibrant coloration, making it visually appealing as well. Brewers primarily use Youngberries in flavored or fruit-infused beers due to their natural sweetness and tanginess. These berries possess high levels of antioxidants and are rich in vitamins A and C, further adding nutritional value to the brews they're incorporated into. Some typical beer styles brewed using Youngberries include wheat beers such as Hefeweizen or Witbier where their bright flavors harmonize beautifully with other ingredients like citrus zest or coriander seeds.

fermentables.name: Yuzu
fermentables.notes: Yuzu, a citrus fruit originating from East Asia, has found its way into the world of beer brewing due to its unique flavor profile. This fruit is known for its aromatic and tangy taste that combines elements of lemon, lime, and grapefruit. When Yuzu is added to beer during the brewing process, it imparts a refreshing and zesty character that enhances the overall taste experience. The influence of Yuzu on beer can vary depending on how it is used. It can be incorporated as juice or zest directly into the brew or added during fermentation to infuse its flavors gradually. Yuzu adds brightness and complexity to beers by complementing hop bitterness with its own natural acidity. Additionally, this fruit brings out floral notes in certain styles while adding a distinctive citrus twist. Brewers use Yuzu for various purposes, ranging from creating new experimental flavors to reinventing classic beer styles. Its properties lend well to both light-bodied lagers and bold IPAs alike. Yuzu 's combination of tartness and sweetness makes it an excellent ingredient for sour beers such as gose or Berliner weisse where it contributes a vibrant citrus kick alongside lactobacillus bacteria's acidity. Moreover, Yuzu finds application in wheat beers like witbier or American pale ale variants where it adds a bright and crisp element that complements the smooth malt base.

yeasts.name: Fermoale
yeasts.notes: Fermoale AY3 is a dry ale yeast from AEB that features high flocculation. The ideal fermentation temperature range for Fermoale AY3 is 14.0-22.0 °C, making it well suited for many styles of beer and other beverages. Its high flocculation properties ensure that only the desired flavors are present in the finished product, while unwanted by-products are efficiently removed. Fermoale AY3 is a reliable choice when brewing any type of ale or lager to provide consistent results with each batch.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Fermoale
yeasts.notes: The Fermoale AY4 yeast from AEB is a dry ale yeast that has a high flocculation and medium alcohol tolerance. It produces a highly attenuated beer, with an attenuation of up to 75%. This yeast works best in the ideal fermentation temperature range of 17.0-25.0°C, making it suitable for most fermentation processes. It is also very tolerant of oxygen levels and can produce good results even when oxygen levels are low.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Fermolager Berlin
yeasts.notes: Fermolager Berlin from AEB is a dry lager yeast that produces an 82.5% attenuation when fermented at 10.0-15.0°C. As a result, this lager yeast creates a crisp and clean flavor profile with minimal fruity esters, making it ideal for producing light and refreshing Pilsners, Lagers and other beers of similar character. Additionally, since Fermolager Berlin ferments at a lower temperature than most ale yeasts, it requires less time to achieve full attenuation, allowing brewers to produce beer quicker without sacrificing quality or flavor complexity.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Fermolager W
yeasts.notes: The Fermolager W of AEB is a dry lager yeast with a high flocculation and alcohol tolerance, ideal for fermenting a variety of beers. It has an attenuation of 87.0% and should be fermented at temperatures between 9.0-15.0 °C in order to get the best results. This yeast will give you consistent, clean beer with excellent flavor and aroma profiles, perfect for lagers and pilsners.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Weiss Arome+
yeasts.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Wheat The Weiss Arome + from AEB is a dry wheat yeast designed for brewing weissbier styles. It has a high flocculation and attenuation of 95%, making it ideal for producing beers with high clarity and crispness. The yeast has an alcohol tolerance up to 12.0% ABV, allowing brewers to push the boundaries of their recipes without worrying about the yeast's ability to ferment. The Weiss Arome + performs best at temperatures between 12.0-25.0 °C, ensuring that brewers can produce consistent quality results every time they brew.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: American Microbrewery Ale
yeasts.notes: The American Microbrewery Ale (A-72) from BSI is a liquid ale yeast with an attenuation of 74.0%. It has high flocculation, medium alcohol tolerance and an ideal fermentation temperature of 17.0-22.0 °C, making it perfect for creating a variety of ales for craft brewers. This versatile strain produces a clean, malty flavor profile with mild fruit esters. It is perfect for traditional American styles such as Pale Ales, IPAs, Amber Ales and more. A-72's quick startup time and reliable performance make it the perfect choice for any craft brewery looking to create flavorful ales quickly and easily.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: American White Ale
yeasts.notes: The American White Ale (A-10) by BSI is an ale yeast strain that produces a liquid form of beer. It has a low flocculation, which helps to keep the beer light and crisp. The attenuation rate of 76.0% allows for an alcohol tolerance of medium, making it ideal for those who enjoy the taste of beer without the strong alcohol content. The ideal fermentation temperature for this ale yeast strain is 16.0-22.0 °C, making it easy to brew in most home brewing setups. This yeast will give your beer a clean and crisp flavor profile with hints of fresh fruit and floral aromas, making it perfect for those who enjoy American-style wheat beers.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Andechs Lager
yeasts.notes: The Andechs Lager from BSI is a liquid lager yeast strain with medium flocculation and alcohol tolerance. With an attenuation of 73.0%, this yeast produces full-bodied beers with good body and mouthfeel. The ideal fermentation temperature for this strain is 10.0-12.0 °C, making it suitable for producing crisp lagers in cooler temperatures. This strain is perfect for producing traditional European-style lagers such as Pilsners, Helles, and Vienna Lagers .
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Andechs Weizen
yeasts.notes: The Andechs Weizen from BSI is a liquid ale yeast that can be used to produce traditional Bavarian-style wheat beers. It has a low flocculation rate and an attenuation of 74.0%, meaning it produces a beer with a full body and high alcohol content. The alcohol tolerance is medium, so it can handle higher alcohol concentrations without sacrificing flavor. For best results, fermentation should occur between 18.0-21.0 °C, allowing for the fullest expression of its intense banana and clove aromas and flavors.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Augustiner Lager
yeasts.notes: The Augustiner Lager from BSI is a liquid lager yeast with a medium flocculation and attenuation level of 73%. Its alcohol tolerance is medium, making it suitable for a variety of beer styles. It ferments best at temperatures between 11.0 and 17.0 °C, giving a balanced flavor profile with crisp malt character and subtle hop presence. This yeast will perform well in all types of beers and can help create delicious lagers for any occasion.

yeasts.name: Belgian Ale
yeasts.notes: The Belgian Ale (ABS3) from BSI is a liquid ale yeast with high flocculation and medium alcohol tolerance. It has an attenuation rate of 74.0%, which results in a full-bodied beer with complex flavors. It ferments best at temperatures between 18.0-24.0°C, allowing brewers to produce traditional Belgian ales with the right balance of aromas, flavors and drinkability.

yeasts.name: British Ale
yeasts.notes: BSI's British Ale (A-98) is a liquid ale yeast with a high flocculation, medium alcohol tolerance, and an ideal fermentation temperature of 18.0-22.0°C. This yeast has an attenuation rate of 74.0%, making it great for creating well rounded full bodied ales with complex flavors and aromas. It can be used in a variety of styles such as English Pale Ales, Browns, Porters and Stouts to create unique and delicious beers that are sure to please any beer enthusiast.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: British Ale II
yeasts.notes: British Ale II (A-35) is a liquid ale yeast produced by BSI. It has a high flocculation rate and an attenuation rate of 74%. It is able to tolerate medium levels of alcohol, and performs best at fermentation temperatures between 17 and 24 degrees Celsius. This yeast can be used to produce ales with a full-bodied flavor that is slightly sweet and fruity.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: British Ale III
yeasts.notes: The British Ale III (A-32) liquid yeast from BSI is a high flocculation ale yeast that can tolerate medium levels of alcohol. It has an attenuation rate of 69.0%, and should be fermented within the ideal temperature range of 16.0-22.0°C for best results. This strain is perfect for producing true English style ales with a balanced flavor profile, and will produce beers with a malty sweetness and subtle fruity undertones.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Chico Ale
yeasts.notes: The Chico Ale (A-56) from BSI is a liquid ale yeast with medium flocculation and medium alcohol tolerance. It has an attenuation of 75.0%, meaning it will provide a good balance between sweetness and dryness. It is designed to ferment best in temperatures between 16.0-22.0 °C, making it suitable for most brewing conditions. The Chico Ale (A-56) from BSI is a great choice for brewers looking for an ale yeast that provides a unique flavor profile without being too overpowering.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: German Ale
yeasts.notes: The German Ale (A-07) from BSI is a liquid ale yeast that has a low flocculation and low alcohol tolerance. It has an attenuation of 75.0% and is best used between 13.0 to 19.0 °C for optimal fermentation. This yeast is a great choice for creating traditional German-style lagers, ales, and wheat beers as it will bring out the subtle flavors of the malt while producing a light, crisp beer that's full of flavor.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: German Lager
yeasts.notes: The German Lager (3470) from BSI is a liquid lager yeast that produces a clean, crisp beer with an excellent balance of malt and hop flavors. It has an attenuation of 75.0%, flocculation of medium, alcohol tolerance of medium, and an ideal fermentation temperature range of 8.0-12.0 °C. This yeast is well suited for producing traditional lagers and pilsners, as well as other styles such as bocks and Oktoberfest beers. With its low fermentation temperatures and high attenuation, it provides the brewer with a consistent, balanced flavor profile in their finished beer.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Henley on Thames Ale
yeasts.notes: The Henley on Thames Ale (A-75) from BSI is a liquid ale yeast with a medium flocculation and an attenuation of 74.0%. It has a medium alcohol tolerance and is best fermented at temperatures between 17.0-22.0°C. This yeast offers a great balance of flavour, producing smooth ales with subtle maltiness, light fruit notes and slight hints of spice. It’s perfect for producing pale ales, brown ales, porters and stouts, as well as other unique styles.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Irish Ale
yeasts.notes: The Irish Ale (A-84) yeast from BSI is a liquid ale yeast that offers an attenuation of 73.0%, flocculation of medium, alcohol tolerance of medium, and ideal fermentation temperature of 18.0-22.0 °C. This yeast is perfect for producing classic Irish ales such as dry stouts and milds. It has a good balance between maltiness and hop character, with subtle nutty notes and a hint of roastiness in the finish. It produces a clean beer with minimal esters and phenols and can ferment at cooler temperatures than most other ale yeasts - making it perfect for producing rich, flavorful beers in a short amount of time!
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Kolsch
yeasts.notes: The Kolsch (A-65) from BSI is a liquid ale yeast that has an attenuation of 75.0%, low flocculation, medium alcohol tolerance, and an ideal fermentation temperature between 12.0 and 18.0 °C. It is a versatile yeast strain suitable for producing a variety of beers ranging from light ales to malty ales and lagers. This strain is also known for its clean flavor profile which allows the unique flavors of each beer to shine through. With its low flocculation and high attenuation, this strain will give you a clean crisp beer with it's classic kolsch flavor characteristics in no time at all!
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: London Ale I
yeasts.notes: The London Ale I (A-28) from BSI is a liquid ale yeast that produces a flavorful beer. This yeast has an attenuation of 75%, a medium flocculation, and a medium alcohol tolerance. It is best fermented at temperatures between 16 and 22 degrees Celsius for optimal results. With its versatile characteristics, London Ale I (A-28) from BSI can be used to produce a variety of ales with great flavor profiles.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: London Ale II
yeasts.notes: The London Ale II (A-68) liquid ale yeast by BSI is a high flocculating strain with an attenuation of 69.0%. This variety has a medium alcohol tolerance and is ideally fermented at temperatures between 18.0-22.0 °C. It produces a smooth and malty flavor profile with subtle notes of fruit esters, making it great for ESB and traditional English ales.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: London Ale III
yeasts.notes: The London Ale III (A-18) from BSI is a liquid ale yeast best suited for making traditional British ales. It has an attenuation of 73%, a medium flocculation, and a medium alcohol tolerance. The ideal fermentation temperature for this yeast is 18.0-23.0 °C, allowing brewers to make balanced and full-flavored beers quickly and easily. This strain produces well-rounded flavors with slight fruitiness, making it an excellent choice for producing classic English ales.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Old German Ale
yeasts.notes: The Old German Ale (A-38) from BSI is a liquid ale yeast perfect for producing classic German-style ales. With an attenuation of 75.0%, this yeast produces a beer that is full in body and malty. It has low flocculation, which helps to create a soft mouthfeel and roundness to the finished product. The alcohol tolerance of this yeast is medium, making it ideal for creating beers with higher ABV levels. The ideal fermentation temperature for this yeast strain is 16.0-22.0 °C, which allows for flexibility when brewing in different environments, but also helps to ensure optimal performance during fermentation.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Pasteur Champagne
yeasts.notes: Pasteur Champagne (1868) by BSI is a liquid wine and cider yeast designed for a variety of alcohol ferments. With an attenuation rate of 68.0%, it produces highly alcoholic drinks with low flocculation qualities. It also has an exceptionally high alcohol tolerance, making it ideal for producing fermented beverages with higher alcohol content. Its optimal fermentation temperature range is from 4.0-34.0°C, making it suitable for use in many different environments and climates. The Pasteur Champagne (1868) yeast is an excellent choice for those seeking to produce high quality alcoholic beverages with robust flavor profiles.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Ringwood Ale
yeasts.notes: Ringwood Ale (1187) from BSI is a liquid form ale yeast with high flocculation and medium alcohol tolerance. It has an attenuation of 72.0% and an ideal fermentation temperature range of 18.0-23.0 °C. This yeast produces fruity esters along with subtle spicy notes, making it an excellent choice for producing traditional English ales or similar styles.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Scotch Ale
yeasts.notes: BSI's Scotch Ale (A-78) is a liquid ale yeast with high attenuation and flocculation levels. It has an alcohol tolerance of up to 8.5%, making it an ideal choice for strong ales, particularly Scotch Ales . The ideal fermentation temperature range for this yeast is 13.0-21.0°C, allowing brewers to make a flavorful beer without having to worry about temperatures that are too hot or cold. While the flavour profile can vary depending on the beer style, this strain will generally produce a malty sweetness with notes of caramel and dark fruit, as well as a hint of smokiness.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Timothy Taylor Ale
yeasts.notes: BSI's Timothy Taylor Ale (A-69) is a high flocculating liquid ale yeast with medium alcohol tolerance. It has an attenuation of 69.0%, making it ideal for producing ales with a full body and pleasant maltiness. Its optimal fermentation temperature range is 18.0 to 22.0 °C, ensuring maximum flavor extraction from the wort. A-69 is versatile enough to produce light beers as well as dark stouts, making it a great choice for brewers looking for consistent results in their brews.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Whitbread Ale
yeasts.notes: The Whitbread Ale (A-99) from BSI is a liquid ale yeast that is known for its high flocculation and low alcohol tolerance. It has an attenuation of 70.0% and works best at fermentation temperatures between 18.0-24.0 °C, making it an ideal choice for producing a rich, full bodied flavor that is perfect for ales of all styles. It's quick to start fermenting and produces consistent results every time, making it one of the most popular yeast varieties on the market.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: American Ale
yeasts.notes: Bio4's American Ale (SY025) is a liquid ale yeast that is highly tolerant of alcohol and has medium flocculation. It has an attenuation rate of 77%, meaning it converts the sugars in your wort into alcohol efficiently. The ideal fermentation temperature for this yeast strain is 15.0-22.0 °C, making it a great choice for producing beers with bright, crisp flavors and aromas. This yeast strain works well in a variety of beer styles from IPAs to pale ales to stouts, making it an excellent choice for homebrewers who want to experiment with different styles of beer.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Heffeweizen Ale
yeasts.notes: Beer Analytics subtype: Wheat Bio4's Hefeweizen Ale (SY055) is a liquid wheat yeast that produces a light and refreshing ale. With an attenuation of 74.0% and low flocculation, this yeast produces a clean, crisp flavor with just the right amount of sweetness. It has a medium alcohol tolerance and is best fermented between 16.0-22.0°C for optimal results. This yeast is perfect for producing fruity aromas and flavors, making it ideal for lighter summer ales or wheat beers with a hint of spice.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: London ESB
yeasts.notes: London ESB (SY030) is a liquid ale yeast from Bio4. This strain produces rich and complex flavors with fruity esters, slightly sweet maltiness and low levels of diacetyl. It has a high flocculation rate, which aids in clarification of the beer. It also has a medium alcohol tolerance and an ideal fermentation temperature range of 18.0-22.0°C. With an attenuation rate of 71%, this strain is great for creating balanced beers with richer malts and hop character.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Norwegian Kveik
yeasts.notes: The Norwegian Kveik (SY081) from Bio4 is a liquid ale yeast strain. It has a medium flocculation and high alcohol tolerance, with an attenuation of 65.0%. This strain is best used at a fermentation temperature between 22.0 and 37.0°C, making it ideal for brewing in warm environments where other yeasts may struggle to ferment properly. It also works well with a variety of beer styles, from ales to IPAs, providing brewers with the flexibility to experiment with different recipes and styles.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Norwegian Kveik 2
yeasts.notes: The Norwegian Kveik 2 (SY084) liquid ale yeast by Bio4 is a high-performance strain, ideal for brewing styles such as ales and lagers. Its high flocculation and attenuation properties, combined with its alcohol tolerance of up to 12%, make it suitable for a range of beer types. It ferments best between 20-37°C, allowing brewers to ferment at higher temperatures than many other yeast strains. This strain produces consistent results in a variety of beers and is perfect for creating complex flavors and aromas in your brews.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Superyeast High Gravity Ale
yeasts.notes: The Superyeast High Gravity Ale (SY042) from Bio4 is a liquid ale yeast designed for high-gravity fermentation. With an attenuation of 80%, the yeast produces full-bodied beers with a medium flocculation rate and a high alcohol tolerance. The optimal fermentation temperature range is 18.0 to 22.0°C, making it ideal for fermenting higher-alcohol ales in warmer temperatures. SY042 is a great choice for brewers looking to craft complex, flavorful high gravity brews.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Aurora
yeasts.notes: The perfect yeast for homebrewers with no temperature control! Use AURORA for worry-free fermentations. Just pitch it and ditch it! AURORA creates pleasant orange and citrus esters that perfectly complement beers like IPAs made with fruit-forward hops. Easily produce rounded, complex beers at temperatures as high as 98F (37C) without being phenolic or having noticeable off flavors. At the high end of fermentation temperature, beers can finish attenuating in as little as three days!
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Aurora BBAUR
yeasts.notes: The Aurora (BBAUR) liquid ale yeast by Bootleg Biology is a high-performance strain with excellent fermentation characteristics. It has an 81.0% attenuation rate, meaning it will convert the majority of sugars into alcohol, and a medium flocculation rate, which results in clear beer with low sediment. This yeast can tolerate up to 13% ABV and ferments best between 24-37°C, allowing brewers to work with a wide range of temperatures for optimal flavour profile. Aurora (BBAUR) is an ideal choice for all types of ale styles, from light ales to dark stouts and everything in between.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Belgian Blend BBXBELG
yeasts.notes: The Belgian Blend (BBXBELG) is a liquid ale yeast produced by Bootleg Biology. This strain has a low flocculation and medium alcohol tolerance, with an ideal fermentation temperature range of 17.0-22.0 °C and an attenuation rate of 72.0%. It produces high esters, phenols and spicy notes, making it ideal for producing Belgian-style beers like tripels, dubbels and saisons . The BBXBELG is known to be consistent and reliable, making it a great choice for homebrewers looking to create delicious Belgian-style beers.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Berliner Blend BBXBRLN
yeasts.notes: Berliner Blend (BBXBRLN) from Bootleg Biology is a liquid form of yeast that is composed of both Brett and bacteria. Its low attenuation rate of 98.0% allows for a very dry beer with high amounts of acidity. This strain also has a low flocculation rating, which results in long fermentation times while still allowing clarity in the finished beer. It has a low alcohol tolerance and should be fermented at temperatures between 18-24°C for best results.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Brulosophy Blend
yeasts.notes: The Brulosophy Blend (BBXBRU1) is a liquid ale yeast created by Bootleg Biology. It is a versatile strain that ferments well in a wide range of temperatures (10.0-20.0 °C). It has low alcohol tolerance, medium flocculation, and an attenuation of 76.0%. This blend is ideal for creating a variety of beer styles, including ales and lagers. Its full flavor profile can be brought out with the right fermentation temperature and will add complexity to your brews.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Chardonnay
yeasts.notes: The Chardonnay (BB99301A) from Bootleg Biology is a liquid wine and cider yeast strain with low flocculation and a 70.0% attenuation rate. It has a medium alcohol tolerance and works best when fermented between 18.0-24.0 °C. This strain produces an estery, fruity aroma and helps to produce bright, sharp flavors in white wines, meads, and ciders. It is well-suited for traditional sparkling wines as well as barrel fermented styles.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Classic American
yeasts.best_for: American Pale Ales, West Coast IPAs, East Coast IPAs, Brut IPAs, Black IPAs & Stouts
yeasts.notes: Professional brewers fondly refer to this culture as Chico. This is THE yeast for recreating authentic hop-forward beer styles like American Pale Ales, West Coast IPAs, East Coast IPAs, Brut IPAs, & Black IPAs. Reliably produces no-nonsense Blonde Ales, American Porters and Stouts. Ideal for fermenting quick sours due to its low pH tolerance. Classic American will delightfully emphasize malt character, the stickiness of hops and the refreshing qualities of bitterness. This culture will not make a pillowy beer.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Classic English
yeasts.best_for: IPA, Pale Ales, Brut IPA, Bitters, Porters & Stouts
yeasts.notes: Classic English produces soft, juicy, and tropical fruit flavors when fermenting beers made with citrusy hops. This culture has become the de facto standard for making hazy New England-style IPAs in addition to the Classic New England culture. Ideal for fermenting Milkshake IPA, Brut IPA and other IPA sub-styles. Traditionally used for making ester-drive Porters, Stouts, Pale Ales, Bitters, and most English-style ales.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts)

yeasts.name: Classic English
yeasts.best_for: IPA, Pale Ales, Brut IPA, Bitters, Porters, Stouts
yeasts.notes: Classic English produces soft, juicy, and tropical fruit flavors when fermenting beers made with citrusy hops. This culture has become the de facto standard for making hazy New England-style IPAs in addition to the Classic New England culture. Ideal for fermenting Milkshake IPA, Brut IPA and other IPA sub-styles. Traditionally used for making ester-drive Porters, Stouts, Pale Ales, Bitters, and most English-style ales.
yeasts.source_names: BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Funk Weapon #1
yeasts.notes: This rare, and commercially unavailable yeast isolate, produces pungent horse blanket and fresh leather aromas. Perfect for breaking out the funk in farmhouse-style beers. Funk Weapon #1 is featured in the Trinity & Epic Brewing collaboration Wild Apple Saison, and Trinity's Magical Brettanomyces Tour #4.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Funk Weapon #2
yeasts.notes: This rare, and commercially unavailable yeast isolate is perfect for 100% Brettanomyces fermentations, especially Brett IPAs. Amplifies citrus and tropical fruit-forward hop flavors and aromas into a punchy ripeness. With extended time under CO2 pressure, pineapple and tropical fruit aromas will be more pronounced. Great for maintaining the nuance of hops in beer with better keeping qualities than a Brewer's Yeast fermentation.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Funk Weapon #3
yeasts.notes: Funk Weapon #3 is a versatile culture that creates wildly different flavor and aroma profiles depending on the age of fermentation. Young fermentations produce mild musty funk and ripe tropical fruit, while older and bottle conditioned ferments show off unique flavors and aromas of strawberry, cherry and tropical candy. This commercially unavailable yeast isolate is ideal for 100% Brettanomyces fermentations or as a secondary strain along with a phenolic Brewer's Yeast culture.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Neepah Blend
yeasts.notes: The NEEPAH IPA Blend is our secret weapon for delivering the juiciest, tropical fruit bomb you've ever made. Carefully cultivated from a special blend of fruit-forward yeast strains, the NEEPAH Blend is here to amplify the gorgeous rainbow of flavors in your New England-Style IPAs by providing an extra punch of danky goodness. Now you can spend less money on expensive hops and spend more time drinking the best made hazy pale in town. Looking for a versatile culture that'll deliver a new take on flavorful English Ales? The NEEPAH Blend creates decadent beers that out class those made with tired ESB strains. This blend works especially well for Brut IPAs, emphasizing the fruity hop character and reducing the perception of bitterness in dry beers.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: NEEPAH Blend BBXNPA
yeasts.notes: The Bootleg Biology NEEPAH Blend (BBXNPA) is a liquid ale yeast strain known for its low attenuation, low flocculation and low alcohol tolerance. It ferments best in temperatures from 19-21°C and produces an estery flavor profile with notes of pineapple, mango and citrus. This strain is perfect for creating tropical and juicy fruit-forward ales that are sure to please any craft beer enthusiast.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Oslo
yeasts.notes: Oslo is a modern take on traditional Norwegian farmhouse brewing cultures. OSLO can comfortably produce beautifully clean, lager-like beers at temperatures as high as 98F (37C) without noticeable off flavors. At the high end of fermentation temperature, beers can finish attenuating in as little as three days! This culture's versatility and neutral flavor profile allows you to effortlessly produce most beer styles. Bootleg is the first yeast lab to release this unique Kveik-family culture sourced from a raw beer made by our good friends at Eik & Tid in Oslo, Norway.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Oslo OSLO
yeasts.notes: Oslo (OSLO) is a liquid ale yeast from Bootleg Biology. With an attenuation of 82.0%, this yeast produces a good balance of malt and hop character, making it suitable for a wide range of brews. It has medium flocculation which helps produce clear beer with good head retention. Oslo has an alcohol tolerance of medium and ferments best at 18-41°C, making it an ideal yeast for brewing in warmer climates.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: S. Arlingtonesis
yeasts.notes: This culture ferments extremely clean in the 50'sF (lagers) & 60'sF (Kolsch and Lager hybrids), and has subtle fruity/citrus esters in the higher end of the Ale fermentation range (wheat-centric beers). May produce sulfur aromas during primary fermentation, but those will be eliminated within a couple weeks (allow longer aging if fermenting at lower temperatures). S. arlingtonesis is a higher attenuator than most ale strains, so adjustments made need to be made to grain bills or mash temperatures if a drier beer is not preferred.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Saison Parfait: New World Saison Blend
yeasts.notes: Saison Parfait pairs classic pepper & spice saison phenolics with prominent juicy fruit esters that evoke citrus and lemon peel, and a touch of banana for complexity. Even more unique, it finishes with a balanced, full-bodied and silky mouthfeel despite its high attenuation. Saison Parfait means the “Perfect Season”, and is our ode to the fall harvest season. A time for hard work and also celebration. The peasants of rural Flanders and Wallonia created the Saison, and what we now call Farmhouse beers, to drink for sustenance and merriment. Bruegel likely depicted the drinking of Saison beer in his classic paintings of rural country life, “The Harvesters” and “Peasant Wedding”.
yeasts.aliases: Saison Parfait; Saison Parfait™: New World Saison Blend
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Sour Solera Blend
yeasts.notes: Sour Solera Blend contains a unique and complex collection of Saccharomyces, Brettanomyces, Lactobacillus, Pediococcus and other funky yeast and souring bacteria pulled from an active fermentation. This blend can sour in a matter of months at 70ºF or higher, or if you prefer a more prolonged fermentation, use large amounts of aged hops and/or ferment and hold at temperatures below 70ºF. This blend is available seasonally, and will always be changing and evolving due to the nature of solera fermentations. Warning: No two Sour Solera Blend releases will be the same, and neither will their fermentations.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Sour Solera Blend BBXSS
yeasts.notes: The Sour Solera Blend (BBXSS) from Bootleg Biology is a liquid form blend of brettanomyces and bacteria that offers high attenuation at 95.0%. With medium flocculation and alcohol tolerance, this strain is ideal for fermentation temperatures between 18.0-24.0 °C. Its low pH and moderate acidity levels make it the perfect choice for adding complexity to your sour beer recipes. It's also capable of producing intense flavors of tropical fruits, stone fruits, and earthy funkiness in a variety of styles including sours, wild ales, fruited beers, and more.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Sour Weapon L
yeasts.notes: If you're looking to drop the pH of wort as quickly and low as possible, Sour Weapon L is your go to Lacto blend. At 98F, we've had trial batches drop the pH of wort to 3.0 after just 24 hours. When pitched at 84F, pH should reach 3.5 in 24 hours. This is the ideal bacteria blend to use for acidifying wort for quick/kettle sours, and is also very effective when co-pitched with a yeast strain. As with any Lactobacillus culture, we recommend only using in wort with zero IBUs as even small amounts of hops may prevent significant souring.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Sour Weapon L BBXSWL
yeasts.notes: The Sour Weapon L (BBXSWL) from Bootleg Biology is a liquid culture of either Brettanomyces or Bacteria, depending on your preference. It has low flocculation, low alcohol tolerance and an ideal fermentation temperature range of 29.0-37.0 °C. This makes it great for sour beers and other fermentables that require a lower temperature to reach their full flavor potential. The Sour Weapon L is perfect for those looking to create unique, flavorful beers with a bit of acidity and funkiness. With its low alcohol tolerance and wide fermentation temperature range, this culture will take your beer to the next level!
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Sour Weapon P
yeasts.notes: We're excited to release our first 100% Lactic Acid Bacteria souring blend! We chose this specific blend because of its ability to sour quickly and cleanly at a range of temperatures, and due to its mild hop tolerance. While not “yeast”, this culture blend of two unique strains of Pediococcus pentosaceus is part of our LYP collection because it was sourced entirely from the wild: an anaerobic malt starter, and flowers from Murfreesboro, TN given to us by our good friend Art Whitaker. Perfect for quickly acidifying unhopped wort for kettle/”quick” sours or co-pitching with yeast.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: The Mad Fermentationist Saison Blend
yeasts.notes: Fine tuned over two years, this blend morphed over time to become an elegant powerhouse of classic Saison spice, stone-fruit Brett, lactic tartness and a dry but well-rounded body. The final master blend consists of Saison yeast, wild Saccharomyces, rare Brettanomyces and an opportunistic Lactobacillus culture. At temperatures as low as 68F (20C) The Mad Fermentationist Saison Blend exhibits a relatively clean primary fermentation profile and high attenuation. Traditional saison temperatures (around 80F/27C) bring out citrus and elevated phenols (pepper and clove). The Brett character shifts depending on wort composition, as maltier beers emphasize cherry and stone fruit qualities. This blend integrates beautifully with fruity and tropical hops, with the unique Brett culture keeping hop aromatics crisp and bright for an extended time. For best results use a highly fermentable wort, dry hopping during the tail of active fermentation, and carbonating naturally.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Blanche
yeasts.notes: Brewferm's Blanche (Y015) is a dry ale yeast with low flocculation. It has an impressive attenuation of 78.0%, making it great for producing beers with a light body and crisp finish. The ideal fermentation temperature for this yeast strain ranges from 18.0-23.0 °C, making it suitable for brewing in a variety of conditions. This strain produces a slightly fruity and spicy aroma but the flavour remains quite neutral, allowing the character of the beer to shine through.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Lager
yeasts.notes: Brewferm's Lager (Y016) is a dry lager yeast with high flocculation. It has an attenuation of 78.0%, and offers optimal fermentation at temperatures between 10.0-15.0 °C. This type of yeast is perfect for making traditional lagers, such as Munich Helles, Oktoberfest style beers, Pilsners, and other light to medium bodied lagers. The flavor profile of this yeast presents a very clean and crisp taste with subtle malt undertones and low bitterness levels that highlight the natural hop aroma in the beer.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Top
yeasts.notes: Brewferm is a dry ale yeast that is perfect for brewing ales and other top-fermented beers. It has a medium-high flocculation rate, an attenuation of 75%, and an alcohol tolerance of medium. It ferments best at temperatures between 18.0 - 25.0 °C, making it ideal for those looking to brew their beer at a moderate temperature. Brewferm is suitable for brewing a wide variety of styles including ales, porters, stouts and wheat beers. With its fast fermentation time, Brewferm is the perfect choice for those looking to quickly enjoy their homebrews.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: CL-0010 American Microbrewery Ale #1

yeasts.name: CL-0020 American Microbrewery Ale #2

yeasts.name: CL-0050 California Pub Ale

yeasts.name: CL-0060 North-Eastern Micro Ale

yeasts.name: CL-0110 British Microbrewery Ale

yeasts.name: CL-0120 British Pale Ale #1

yeasts.name: CL-0130 British Pale Ale #2

yeasts.source_names: Wall Brew Co common-beer-data

yeasts.name: CL-0150 British Real Ale
yeasts.notes: Great for real pub bitters. Has a complex, woody flavor and musty ester profile that characterizes real ale. Underattenuating to leave mild sweetness to the finish.
yeasts.source_names: Wall Brew Co common-beer-data

yeasts.name: CL-0160 British Draft Ale
yeasts.notes: Full bodied, well rounded ale yeast with a touch of diacytl. Emphasizes malt character. Great for porters and bitters.

yeasts.name: CL-0170 Classic British Ale

yeasts.name: CL-0200 Scottish Ale

yeasts.name: CL-0260 Canadian Ale

yeasts.name: CL-0270 Australian Ale

yeasts.name: CL-0300 Belgian Ale #1

yeasts.name: CL-0340 Belgian Ale #3

yeasts.name: CL-0380 Saison

yeasts.name: CL-0600 Original Pilsner

yeasts.name: CL-0620 American Megabrewery
yeasts.notes: Smooth yeast with a slight fruity flavor. Lagers into a smooth, clean tasting beer. Use for light, clean lager styles with unobtrusive yeast character.

yeasts.name: CL-0630 American Microbrewery Lager
yeasts.notes: Strong fermenter. Leaves a clean, full flavored, malty finish. Slightly attenuative. Versatile for most lager styles with a clean full flavor.

yeasts.name: CL-0650 Old Bavarian Lager

yeasts.name: CL-0680 East European Lager

yeasts.name: Amber Lager
yeasts.notes: The Amber Lager (B38) from Bulldog is a dry lager yeast with high flocculation and medium alcohol tolerance. This robust yeast strain produces malty beer with a full, creamy body and subtle fruitiness. The ideal fermentation temperature for this strain is 9.0-14.0 °C, and it has an attenuation of 73.0%. This yeast produces beers that are complex yet balanced and highly drinkable, making it a great choice for any amber lager or bock style beer.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: American West
yeasts.notes: The American West (B5) strain of Bulldog dry ale yeast is a medium flocculating yeast with an attenuation of 73.0%. It has a medium alcohol tolerance and is best used at temperatures between 16.0-21.0 °C for optimal fermentation and flavor development. This strain produces a light, clean finish and is great for any American-style ales, especially those with citrus or tropical fruit notes. For brewers looking to make classic American styles, this is the perfect choice!

yeasts.name: Bavarian Wheat

It has a low flocculation rate and a medium alcohol tolerance, and it ferments best at temperatures between 18.0-25.0 °C with an attenuation of 78.0%. This strain is perfect for producing classic German wheat beers with a rich banana and clove profile in the finished product. Its low flocculation helps to create a beer with a hazy appearance, while its high attenuation allows for an enjoyable dry finish.

yeasts.name: Belgian Saison
yeasts.notes: The Belgian Saison (B16) from Bulldog is a dry ale yeast with medium flocculation and high alcohol tolerance. It has an attenuation of 85.0% and is best fermented at a temperature of 18.0-30.0°C. This yeast strain produces esters, which gives the beer fruity aromas, as well as spicy phenols that add complexity to the flavor profile. This yeast works particularly well for creating traditional Belgian Saison beers, but can also be used in other styles such as IPAs and pale ales.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Belgian Trappix
yeasts.notes: The Belgian Trappix (B19) strain from Bulldog is a dry ale yeast that has a high flocculation and medium alcohol tolerance. It has an excellent attenuation of 78.0%, which helps to create beers with a nice balance between sweetness and bitterness. The ideal fermentation temperature for B19 is 18.0-25.0 °C, so brewers should strive to keep their fermenting beer in this range to achieve the best flavor and aroma profile from the yeast. This strain produces complex aromatic compounds that add depth and complexity to any beer it ferments, making it an ideal choice for Belgian style ales, witbiers, and saisons .
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: English Ale
yeasts.notes: Bulldog's English Ale (B4) is a dry ale yeast with high flocculation and medium alcohol tolerance. It has an attenuation of 67.0%, making it a great option for creating a full-bodied beer. This yeast is best fermented at 16.0-21.0 °C, allowing for complex esters to develop in the finished beer without becoming overly fruity. This yeast is perfect for producing traditional British ales such as bitters, porters, and milds.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: European Ale
yeasts.notes: European Ale (B44) from Bulldog is a dry and highly flocculated ale yeast with medium alcohol tolerance. It has an attenuation of 73.0%, making it ideal for producing a variety of European-style ales including lagers, pilsners, bocks and malty beers. The ideal fermentation temperature for this yeast is 15.0-21.0 °C, making it suitable for use in most home brewing environments. This yeast will produce a clean finish with little ester production and minimal unwanted flavors.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: German Lager
yeasts.notes: German Lager (B34) from Bulldog is a dry lager yeast that features a high flocculation, medium alcohol tolerance and an ideal fermentation temperature of 9.0-14.0 °C. It has an attenuation of 78.0%, making it a great choice for creating light and crisp beers with a clean finish. This yeast is perfect for making traditional German lagers, as well as other European lagers and light ales.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Steam Lager
yeasts.notes: The Steam Lager (B23) from Bulldog is a dry lager yeast that produces a high flocculation and medium alcohol tolerance. This strain is best used at temperatures between 13.0 to 20.0°C and has an attenuation of 78.0%. It is perfect for brewing traditional German-style lagers with a clean, crisp finish. With its easy fermentation process, this strain is ideal for beginner brewers who want to make a classic lager beer with good flavor and aroma.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Universal Ale
yeasts.notes: The Bulldog Universal Ale (B01) is a dry ale yeast that is great for making classic ales. It has an attenuation of 73.0%, meaning it ferments the sugars in the wort to create a beer with medium body and lower alcohol content. This yeast also has medium flocculation, which helps give the beer a good clarity, as well as aid in creating a good head retention. The ideal fermentation temperature for this yeast is 18-23°C - any cooler and it will take longer to ferment, and any warmer might cause off-flavors or other issues. It also has a medium alcohol tolerance, so beers brewed with this yeast can have up to 6-7% ABV without any problems.

yeasts.name: Coopers Ale
yeasts.notes: Coopers Ale is a dry ale yeast that is known for its high flocculation and medium alcohol tolerance. This yeast is perfect for creating classic British-style ales, such as Pale Ales, English IPA 's, and Nut Brown Ales . It produces a clean flavor profile with subtle notes of fruit, spice, and hops that leave a smooth finish. Coopers Ale also works well in combination with other yeasts to add complexity to your brews.

yeasts.name: Abbey's Sellection

It has an alcohol tolerance of 12.0% and is best used at temperatures between 19.0-24.0°C, making it suitable for brewing a range of ales such as Belgian Witbiers, Belgian Dubbel, or Belgian Tripels . This yeast will allow your beer to have improved body and flavor compared to other yeasts in its class.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: American Cream
yeasts.notes: The American Cream (CL014) liquid ale yeast from Crescat Labs is a great choice for those looking to achieve a unique flavor profile. The alcohol tolerance of 10.0% ensures that you can brew just about any style beer without worrying about the yeast going dormant during fermentation. Best of all, it ferments best at temperatures between 14.0-22.0 °C, making it ideal for brewing year-round in warmer climates. Whether you're looking for an easy drinking pale ale or a full bodied stout, the American Cream from Crescat Labs has everything you need to make a delicious brew every time!
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Bagpipes Chanter

This strain is best used at temperatures of 18-22°C for optimal fermentation. It has been designed to give a classic flavor profile while producing a very clean finish. Additionally, this strain provides excellent foam stability and can be used in almost any beer style. With its balanced malt flavor and estery character, the Bagpipes Chanter will help make your beer stand out from the rest!
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Bayernfest

This strain has an alcohol tolerance of 11% and ferments best between 8.0-14.0°C, making it perfect for producing flavorful, yet clean lagers that are true to the traditional German recipe.

yeasts.name: Belgian Meander

Belgian Meander (CL008) is known for producing fruity esters that add complexity to beer, making it a popular choice among homebrewers and craft brewers alike.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Black Clover

yeasts.name: Cologne Definition

The CL013 yeast produces a dry and robust flavor profile with a clean finish, making it ideal for many beer styles.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Flemish Rhapsody

It is perfect for crafting a wide variety of Belgian beer styles including saisons, dubbels, tripels, quads, and witbiers as well as sours such as lambics and Flanders red ales . This versatile strain will produce complex flavors of fruit esters and spicy phenolics that are characteristic of traditional Belgian beers.

yeasts.name: Friar's Strong

Friar's Strong is ideal for producing strong ales and Belgian beers with delightful esters and complex aromas.

yeasts.name: Kveik & Fox

yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: London's Calling

Its high attenuation makes it great for producing clean malt flavors and aromas, while its low alcohol tolerance makes it perfect for producing classic English ales without too much alcohol content. yeasts.name: Moravian Vale

yeasts.name: Piwo Cells

yeasts.name: Saison's Season

yeasts.name: Trapeze Trappist
