It has a high flocculation rate and an alcohol tolerance of up to 10.0%, making it ideal for stronger beers. This yeast works best when fermented at temperatures between 18.0-22.0 °C and is perfect for producing a smooth, full-bodied beer with plenty of hop aroma and flavor.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Kveik
yeasts.notes: Mangrove Jack's Kveik (M12) is a dry ale yeast strain that is well-suited for brewing a wide variety of beer styles. It has high flocculation and a high alcohol tolerance, making it suitable for brewing high-alcohol beers. Ideal fermentation temperatures range from 20.0°C to 40.0°C, making it an ideal choice for brewers in hot climates. The unique flavor profile of this strain adds notes of tropical fruit, citrus, and spice to the finished beer. It can be used to brew a wide range of styles including IPAs, saisons, sours, Belgian ales, and many more.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Liberty Bell Ale
yeasts.best_for: Pale Ales, Extra Special Bitters & Golden Ales
yeasts.notes: A top fermenting ale yeast suitable for a wide variety of hoppy and distinctive style beers. This strain produces light, delicate fruity esters and helps to develop malt character.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Mead
yeasts.notes: Mangrove Jack's Mead (M05) is a dry wine and cider yeast that offers a high attenuation of 97.5%. It has a medium-high flocculation rate, making it an ideal choice for mead fermentation. In terms of temperature, its optimal range is 15.0-30.0°C, allowing brewers to ferment their mead in a wide variety of temperatures depending on their desired flavor profile. This yeast strain is great for creating crisp and clear meads with intense aromas and flavors.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: New World Strong Ale
yeasts.notes: A top-fermenting ale strain suitable for many types of ales of all strengths. Ferments with a neutral yeast aroma to ensure the full character of the malts and hops are prominent in each beer.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: UK Dark Ale
yeasts.notes: Mangrove Jack's UK Dark Ale (M03) is a dry ale yeast that is known for its medium flocculation and high attenuation of 73.0%. It is best to ferment this yeast in temperatures between 18.0-22.0 °C for optimal performance and flavor. This yeast provides a full-bodied, malty beer with an authentic English character and subtle fruitiness, making it the perfect choice for creating traditional British ales and bitters .
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: US West Coast
yeasts.best_for: Americal Pale Ale, Double IPA, American Imperial Stout
yeasts.notes: Mangrove Jack's US West Coast (M44) is a dry ale yeast renowned for its versatile usage across various beer styles. With an impressive attenuation of 78.0%, it ensures that most of the sugars in the wort get converted into alcohol, resulting in a more dry and less sweet beer. Its high flocculation property ensures that yeast cells clump together and settle at the bottom of the fermenter, leaving a clear beer with less sediment. This yeast thrives at an ideal fermentation temperature range of 59.0-73.4°F (15.0-23.0°C), allowing for a broad spectrum of brewing environments. It is commonly used in crafting typical beer styles like American Pale Ale, American IPA, and other US-style ales, where its characteristic performance helps shape the desired outcome. The US West Coast (M44) yeast imparts a neutral flavor profile, thus allowing the hop character and the malt backbone of the beer to shine through, contributing to its popularity among home and craft brewers alike.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Workhorse Beer
yeasts.notes: Mangrove Jack's Workhorse Beer (M10) is a dry ale yeast that produces a strong, full-bodied flavor. With an attenuation rate of 78%, this yeast produces a light-colored beer with plenty of body and flavor. It has a medium flocculation rate, meaning it settles out of suspension well and produces a clear beer with plenty of carbonation. The ideal fermentation temperature for this yeast is 15.0-20.0°C, producing the best balance between ester formation and attenuation rates for optimal flavors and aromas in your finished beer.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Gervin Ale
yeasts.notes: Muntons Gervin Ale (GV-12) is a dry ale yeast with low flocculation and low alcohol tolerance. It offers an attenuation of 70.0%, creating a full body beer that still maintains a refreshing taste. This yeast is best used at temperatures between 16.0-22.0 °C for optimal fermentation and flavor development. Gervin Ale (GV-12) is a great choice for making light ales, such as pale ales and IPAs, that have a balanced sweetness and bitterness.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Muntons Premium Gold
yeasts.best_for: The functional properties of brewing yeasts have a direct impact on the performance, quality and economics of the resulting beer.
yeasts.notes: Muntons Premium Gold brewer's yeast has proved itself for many years as a particular favorite for brewers of all malt beer recipes or recipes that call for a high percentage of malt in the grist formulation. It has the ability to resist ‘sticking' a problem often experienced with all malt recipe beers. And it has excellent crusting characteristics; the yeast residue sticks to the bottom of the fermenter, bottle or pressure barrel in a firm mass, resisting disturbance, meaning you get more beer, less waste.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Muntons Standard Ale
yeasts.notes: Muntons brewer's yeast has been a popular favourite for many years amongst the homebrew community worldwide, gaining an enviable reputation for its consistent healthy performance, its hardy nature and its clean finish. Muntons brewer's yeast is a dried brewer's yeast that produces a powdery flocculation with an apparent attenuation of 70%. Ideal fermentation temperature is between 64° - 70°F to produce an alcohol tolerance of 8% ABV. It provides low ester formation but with relatively high residual sugar giving good body and mouth feel.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Abbey Ale C
yeasts.notes: The Abbey Ale C's Trappist origin is best coupled with a little monastic patience: a notably low-flocculator, it is highly attenuating, with a fruity profile and lightly perceptible spiciness, as well as often significant banana character.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: All The Bretts
yeasts.notes: An evolving blend of many of the Brett strains in the Omega collection. Use this yeast in the secondary and expect high attenuation and a fruity and funky complexity that continues to develop over time.
yeasts.aliases: ALL THE BRETTS; All the Bretts
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Alt
yeasts.notes: An enthusiastic top cropper from Düsseldorf. This strain ferments at low temperatures with a clean, low ester profile. Light fruit emerges at higher temperatures. Features quick maturation. Yeast stays in suspension. Little to no diacetyl. Try also Kolsch II (OYL-044) or even West Coast Ale I (OYL-004)
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: American Lager
yeasts.notes: This strain is thought to be from one of the US's oldest family-owned breweries in Minnesota. More flocculent and complex in flavor than many of its lager peers, including American Pilsner (OYL-102).
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: American Pilsner
yeasts.notes: Thought to be from the most popular beer in America. A mild, neutral, smooth lager strain, dry and clean with good malt and very slight apple characteristics.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: American Wheat
yeasts.notes: Energetically top cropping, this powerful fermenter leaves behind a light, tart and refreshing, crisp character. Fairly clean and lightly dry, it excels particularly at American styles. The small amount of sulfur produced during fermentation conditions out.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Bavarian Wheat I
yeasts.notes: A spicier alternative to Hefeweizen Ale I (OYL-021) for the production of German wheat beers, Bavarian Wheat I imparts a more phenolic profile with predominant notes of clove and pepper.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Bavarian Wheat II
yeasts.notes: A big top cropper and a low flocculator, with banana, light pear, apple/plum, clove and vanilla. Another great wheat beer option with a more complex aroma relative to Hefeweizen Ale I (OYL-021). Up the esters with higher temperatures, wort density and lower pitch rate, or keep muted at lower temperatures to show clove. Sulfur conditions out.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Bayern Lager
yeasts.notes: Thought to come from Munich's oldest, traditional and vintage-vibed brewery. This clean, crisp, lager strain ferments well at a wide range, has good flocculation, and has both low sulfur and low diacetyl production.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Belgian Ale A
yeasts.notes: As one of the few highly flocculent Belgian ale strains, this strain makes a great Belgian house strain. It is brewery friendly, crops easily and has a well-rounded flavor profile with balanced fruitiness and phenolics. Esters increase with upward temperatures.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Belgian Ale D
yeasts.notes: This devil of a strain is thought to be from the famous strong golden ale brewer. The bargain is classic sacrifice for pay off: tricky fermentation kinetics for rich flavor profile and aroma complexity. If tempted by this flavorful but low flocculating stop-and-starter, let us know and we can help with a tip or two. Belgian Golden Strong (OYL-056) is a great alternative with a similar flavor profile, but more reliable fermentation performance.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Belgian Ale DK
yeasts.notes: A mild Belgian-charactered ale yeast with light toasty or biscuit-like aromatic maltiness. Can produce a touch of lagery sulfur, which conditions out over time.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Belgian Ale O
yeasts.notes: With balanced fruit and phenolics, this Trappist ale yeast's clean and dry profile carries a signature sharp tasting, slightly acidic finish that the thought-to-be brewery of origin describes as acidulous. Welcomes high gravity. Belgian profile is toned down compared to Abbey Ale C (OYL-018) and Belgian Ale W (OYL-028).
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Belgian Ale R
yeasts.notes: This has low phenolics for a Belgian strain, with stone fruit and light, floral or rose-like aromas. Sulfur produced dissipates with conditioning. Accentuated flavors and aromas occur at higher temps, and in a high gravity environment.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Belgian Ale W
yeasts.notes: An eruptive top cropper displaying nice fruit and rustic phenolics. This reliable Belgian strain is a good flocculator with a wide temperature range. Three famous brewers ferment this on vastly different schedules, showing the varied outcomes available.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Belgian Dark Ale A
yeasts.notes: Omega Yeast Labs' Belgian Dark Ale A (OYL-040) is a liquid ale yeast that offers a high alcohol tolerance and a medium flocculation. It has an attenuation of 76.5%, and the ideal fermentation temperature for this yeast strain is between 18.0-27.0 °C. This strain produces subtly spicy, fruity esters that pair well with the dark malts used in Belgian ales, making it an excellent choice for any homebrewer looking to create a classic Belgian dark ale.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Belgian Golden Strong
yeasts.notes: Perfectly suited for the production of high-gravity Belgian ales where a dry finish is desired. A mellow phenolic character is balanced by an ester profile of pear and light banana, while high levels of glycerol production ensure a round mouthfeel even at very low finishing gravity. Consistently reaches greater than 90 apparent attenuation without sluggishness or stalling.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Belgian Saison I
yeasts.notes: Well regarded as a farmhouse ale strain despite fickle fermentation behavior. It has fruity complexity, good phenolics and a tart and dry finish. It's better at warm fermentation temperatures, but is still well known to stall around 1.030. Try using an additional strain to aid attenuation, or the more reliable Saisonstein's Monster (OYL-500), Belgian Saison II (OYL-042) or French Saison (OYL-026).
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Belgian Saison II
yeasts.notes: Thought to originate from a small, sophisticated, Belgian brewer's spelt saison. It is earthy, spicy, peppery, tart and dry, with tropical fruit and citrus at warm fermentation temperatures. A perfect strain for farmhouse ales and saisons. It favors pitching in the upper 60s or low 70s, and free-rising from there.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Belgian Wheat
yeasts.notes: This strain is great for a wheat beer with more ester complexity than Hefeweizen Ale I (OYL-021) and Hefeweizen Ale II (OYL-022). The strain features apple, bubblegum, plum, and a lightly tart and dry finish. It supports malt and hop flavors well.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Biere De Garde
yeasts.best_for: Ales, Farmhouse, Bière de Garde & Saison
yeasts.notes: Lightly phenolic, fruity, dry, delicately tart and a very low flocculator, this presents much like a saison strain. Try this for Bière de Garde, or a Belgian or French farmhouse ale. In fact, a clean-bodied Bière de Garde can be achieved with any lager strain here at the warm end of its temperature range. For farmhouse, try also French Saison (OYL-026) or Belgian Saison II (OYL-042)
yeasts.aliases: BIERE DE GARDE; Biere de Garde
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Brett Blend #1 Where Da Funk?
yeasts.notes: One Brett-famous Colorado brewery strain plus two uniquely funky Sacch strains result in huge tropical fruit aroma (fades a bit during conditioning) with a wide temperature range. Very dry (consider flaked oats for body). Develops mild funk and low acid even with extended aging. Pairs well with fruity aroma hops for a unique pale ale.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Brett Blend #2 Bit O' Funk
yeasts.notes: This blend contains the two Saccharomyces strains from Brett Blend #1 for primary fermentation and is spiked with Brettanomyces Bruxellensis (OYL-202) for development of moderate funk during a secondary fermentation. The bit ‘o funkiness will take extended time (3+ months) to develop.
yeasts.aliases: BRETT BLEND #2 BIT O'FUNK; Brett Blend #2 Bit O'Funk
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Brett Blend #3 Bring On Da Funk
yeasts.notes: Two Sacch strains from Brett Blend #1 (OYL-210) spiked with both brux and lambicus, plus two additional Brett isolates from a Brett-famous Colorado brewery, plus two Brett isolates from an intense Belgian source equals a funky, fruity, complex, 8-strain composition. Brett character develops over time (as will acid production if exposed to oxygen)
yeasts.aliases: BRETT BLEND #3 BRING ON DA FUNK
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Brettanomyces Bruxellensis
yeasts.notes: First classified in 1904, Bretts are crucial in secondary fermentation for Belgian styles, consuming sugars that Sacchs leave behind. Brett Bruxellensis contributes medium Brett intensity with classic barnyard earthiness and a light medicinal quality. See also: Brett Claussenii (OYL-201), Brett Lambicus (OYL-203), and three Funk blends (OYL-210, 211, 212).
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Brettanomyces Claussenii
yeasts.notes: The mildest on the Brett funkiness spectrum, Brett Claussenii presents more of a leathery earthiness and some pineapple—both characteristics that are contributed in large part by the aroma alone. It does its best work as a secondary yeast. See also: Brett Bruxellensis (OYL-202), Brett Lambicus (OYL-203) and three Funk blends (OYL-210, 211, 212)
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Brettanomyces Lambicus
yeasts.notes: Dive in deep with horsey, spicy, cherry pie funk in this significant Brett strain— best in secondary pitches. See also: Brett Bruxellensis (OYL-202), Brett Claussenii (OYL-201), three Funk blends (OYL-210, 211, 212), All The Bretts (OYL-218) or our farmhouse blend: C2C Farmhouse (OYL-217).
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: British Ale I
yeasts.notes: A productive, brewery friendly, top cropper attributed to a historic London brewery whose lab once hosted Louis Pasteur. It drops fast and clear, and is clean and crisp at low temperatures with heightened esters and a lightly tart, dry finish at upper ranges. Try also British Ale II (OYL-007) for less attenuation and enhanced malts, or British VIII (OYL-016)
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: British Ale II
yeasts.notes: Like British Ale I (OYL-006), this English brewery strain is thought to be from the historical London brewery that Louis Pasteur visited. It is a strong fermenter, brewery friendly, flexible, leaves near spotless clarity, and has more fruit-like esters and malt than British Ale I. Select for malt and fruit at higher fermentation temperatures or a clean profile at lower temperatures.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: British Ale III
yeasts.notes: This is a top cropping, complex and malty strain. A shy starter, it's slow but steady to ferment and a notorious diacetyl maker. Despite its finicky nature, its noteworthy esters match well with English style ales. It is highly flocculent and clears extremely well without filtration.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: British Ale IV
yeasts.notes: Nuances of apple, clover honey and pear and a light mineral quality for great character presentation in English styles, particularly bitters. Not very flocculent compared to a lot of English strains. Filtration recommended.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: British Ale V
yeasts.best_for: Ale, British Ales, IPA & Hazy IPA
yeasts.notes: A good top cropper thought to be from a famous Manchester bitters maker. Its residual sweetness pairs popularly with the signature huge, fruity hop flavor and aroma of the NEIPA. Alternately, try DIPA (OYL-052) for slightly less residual sweetness
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: British Ale VI
yeasts.notes: British Ale VI sports a classic British character—reserved but witty, with a rather high tolerance for alcohol. Crisp, clean, malty and with a mostly dry finish. A good flocculator.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: British Ale VII
yeasts.notes: A well behaved, reasonably productive flocculator that leaves a clear bodied beer. This strain produces very clean, well balanced ales that are both significantly malty and have esters reminiscent of stone fruit with dry, nutty tones at the back end. Think compatibility with cask ales, for example.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: British Ale VIII
yeasts.notes: A ridiculously thorough flocculator thought to be from a highly regarded English ESB. This strain has unique fruitiness and noticeable finishing sweetness. Drops out quickly and completely. Easy to crop, but needs a diacetyl rest. To enhance the fruit, ferment up at the recommended temperature ceiling.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: British Ale XI
yeasts.notes: The British Ale XI (OYL-048) liquid ale yeast from Omega Yeast Labs is a versatile and reliable strain for brewing a wide variety of traditional British ales. This strain has an impressive 77% attenuation, resulting in clean, well-attenuated beer with good malt character. It flocculates out very well, making it ideal for clear beers, while its high alcohol tolerance makes it great for brewing strong ales . The optimal fermentation temperature range is 19.0-21.0 °C, allowing brewers to control the balance between fruity and estery aromas and flavors.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: British Cask
yeasts.notes: The British Cask (OYL-038) from Omega Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast suitable for a variety of beer styles. It has an impressive attenuation of 75.5%, a high flocculation, and a medium alcohol tolerance. The ideal fermentation temperature range for this strain is between 17.0-22.0 °C, giving brewers enough flexibility to produce the desired beer characteristics in their finished product. This yeast strain can be used to create classic English ales with notes of biscuit and toast, as well as fruity esters when fermented at the higher end of its temperature range.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: C2C American Farmhouse
yeasts.notes: A coast to coast blend of one saison strain from a famous Northeast U.S. brewery and one Brett strain from a Northwest U.S. brewery. The blend results in a fast developing fruity and funky farmhouse ale.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts)

yeasts.name: C2C American Farmhouse
yeasts.notes: The C2C American Farmhouse (OYL-217) liquid yeast strain from Omega Yeast Labs is a brett or bacteria strain that offers great flavor and aroma complexity. This strain has an attenuation rate of 78%, low flocculation, an alcohol tolerance of up to 10%, and the ideal fermentation temperature range lies between 20-27 °C. It is well suited for producing saisons, farmhouse ales, Belgian ales, and sour beers. The C2C American Farmhouse (OYL-217) will help you achieve the perfect balance between tartness and funkiness in your brews!
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: CL-50 Ale
yeasts.best_for: Pale Ale, Brown Ale, Red Ale, IPA, Stout, Porter & Cream Ale
yeasts.notes: Producing a notably big-body and soft texture, this versatile, well-attenuating strain's profile is a launch pad for the gamut of malt and hop characteristics. It achieves substantial maltiness without being overly sweet.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Danish Lager
yeasts.notes: A powdery low flocculator, this strain produces a crisp and dry, soft and round profile that's great for supporting hop flavors. Ferments relatively cool and has low attenuation. Allow for long conditioning to help clear. Good in Dortmund lagers, Munich helles, and American lagers.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Dipa Ale
yeasts.notes: A strong fermenter popularly referred to as Conan. Its peach, apricot and pineapple notes are steroids for hops, complementing modern fruity hop profiles in particular. A diacetyl rest is suggested if fermented in the lower temperature range.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: East Coast Ale
yeasts.notes: Thought to be the famous Bostonian strain. It is suitable for a broad range of beer styles with an American spin. Using West Coast Ale I (OYL-004) for comparison, it is a little tart and slightly muting of hop bitterness. Slightly less flocculent and attenuating, too, but every bit as versatile, carrying an overall clean and neutral flavor character.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Espe Kveik
yeasts.best_for: Kveik, American IPA, Hazy IPA, American Pale Ale, Black IPA, Red IPA, Red Ale, Robust Porter, American Stout, Winter Seasonal Beer, English IPA, Extra Special Bitter, Bitter, Stout, Tropical, Blonde Ale, American Strong Ale, Cream Ale, American Amber Lager, American Brown Ale, White IPA & Imperial IPA
yeasts.notes: Originating from the village of Grodås in Norway, Espe offers the unique profile of lychee, pear, and tropical fruit cup. The strain bolsters the sweet aromatics of modern IPAs, but is versatile enough for your flagship pale ale or seasonal brew. Espe is most expressive when fermented at 90°F+ (32°C+), but still reveals its character at lower ale-pitching temperatures.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: French Saison
yeasts.notes: This citrusy, lightly phenolic saison strain is so attenuative and reliable in performance that people joke it could ferment a shoe. The French Saison strain results in great body consistency. It is good for any of the characteristically aromatic Belgian styles and is highly compatible with hops and spice aromas.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: German Bock
yeasts.notes: Thought to be from the famous Alpine brewery in Aying, Bavaria. This is a versatile, malty-charactered lager strain that balances malt and hop flavors well. It is superb for bocks, doppelbocks, Oktoberfest lagers, helles and a favorite for American pilsners, too.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: German Lager I
yeasts.notes: Versatile, crisp, malty profile, light esters and a wide fermentation range. This is thought to be the world's most used lager strain and can produce a convincing lager at ale temperatures. Fermenting in the low temperature range (45-55), it maintains a more crisp profile. Temperatures higher in range (65-68) bring out slightly heightened esters. Rest for diacetyl.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: German Lager II
yeasts.notes: Great for Bavarian styles. A confident fermenter with good attenuation resulting in a smooth, full-bodied, malty finish and balanced aroma. Slight sulfur and low diacetyl.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Grand Cru
yeasts.notes: Made for wits or any other Belgian ale—even sweet mead or cider—this strain's clove phenolics, esters and tart and dry ending was historically enhanced by orange peel and coriander. The well-known Belgian wheat beer was brought back from extinction in its historic home of Hoegaarden by Pierre Celis, from which this strain is thought to come.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Gulo Ale
yeasts.best_for: Saison, Ales, IPA, Brut IPA, Stout & Bière de Garde
yeasts.notes: Gulo Ale is the latest creation to emerge from the curious minds of our R&D team. The progeny of Irish Ale (OYL-005) and French Saison (OYL-026), this true genetic hybrid is a beast at devouring sugars, which creates a very dry beer without any of the peppery, clove phenolics associated with saisons and Belgian ales. Expect a citrus-forward aroma with hints of peach and a clean finish. Gulo Ale excels in any style where a high level of attenuation is desired without phenolics. We love using it in an IPA (including a brut IPA), stout, or Bière de Garde. Non-phenolic.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Hefeweizen Ale I
yeasts.notes: A classic German wheat strain, it's a cloudy, big top cropper. Presenting banana and clove, the esters turn up with increased temperatures, wort density and decreased pitch rate, or stay muted at lower temperatures where clove stands out. Over pitching can lessen the banana. Sulfur conditions out. See also Belgian Ale A (OYL-024) for an alternate complexity.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Hefeweizen Ale II
yeasts.notes: Identical to Hefeweizen Ale I (OYL-021) except flocculent, Hefeweizen Ale II produces a crystal clear body with no additional steps and is a big top cropper. Up esters with upper fermentation temperatures, wort density and decreased pitch rate, or keep esters muted to let clove show. Turn down banana by over pitching. Sulfur conditions out.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Hornindal Kveik
yeasts.best_for: Kveik, American IPA, Hazy IPA, American Pale Ale, Black IPA, Red IPA, Red Ale, Robust Porter, American Stout, Winter Seasonal Beer, English IPA, Extra Special Bitter, Bitter, Stout, Tropical, Blonde Ale, American Strong Ale, Cream Ale, American Amber Lager, American Brown Ale, White IPA & Imperial IPA
yeasts.notes: A wonderfully unique Norwegian farmstead kveik, Hornindal produces a tropical flavor and complex aroma that can present itself as stonefruit, pineapple, and dried fruit leather, which complement fruit-forward hops. Add even more dimension to C hops and increase ester intensity with a high fermentation temperature. Ferments well at 90°F+. Non-phenolic and no fusels, even at higher temperatures.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Hothead Ale
yeasts.best_for: Kveik, American IPA, Hazy IPA, American Pale Ale, Black IPA, Red IPA, Red Ale, Robust Porter, American Stout, Winter Seasonal Beer, English IPA, Extra Special Bitter, Bitter, Stout, Tropical, Blonde Ale, American Strong Ale, Cream Ale, American Amber Lager, American Brown Ale, White IPA & Imperial IPA
yeasts.notes: A highly flocculent Norwegian ale strain with an astoundingly wide temperature range and little change in flavor across the range. Clean enough for both American and English styles, it has a unique honey-like aroma with overripe mango. Complementary to modern, fruity hops. Temperature control is unnecessary with this strain. Non-phenolic and no fusels, even at higher temperatures
yeasts.aliases: HOTHEAD ALE; HotHead Ale; Hothead Ale
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Irish Ale
yeasts.notes: Ireland's storied stout is thought to be balanced by this dry, crisp, lightly fruity, versatile and powerful strain. A good fermenter with reliable, average flocculation (some diacetyl possible), and a hint of fruit at the lowest recommended temperatures, which increases in complexity at higher temperatures (64+). Successful in dark and high gravity beers. Sláinte!
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Jovaru Lithuanian Farmhouse
yeasts.notes: Borne from an exclusive partnership with the famed Jovaru Brewery's queen of Lithuanian farmhouse beer, this unique yeast complements farmhouse beers with citrusy esters and restrained phenols. The strain produces a character of lemon pith, black pepper, and a soft mouthfeel.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Kolsch I
yeasts.notes: An enthusiastically top cropping, lager-like ale strain from Koln, Kolsch I is lightly fruity, crisp and clean, and accentuates hop flavors well. This strain can be fermented colder than Kolsch II (OYL- 044), and is powdery and slow to drop clear (filtering recommended). Kolsch II (OYL-044) is a little easier to manage. Sulfur disappears with age.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Kolsch II
yeasts.notes: This Kolsch strain is warmer fermenting than Kolsch I (OYL-017), flocculates much better and clears more quickly, so is a little easier to manage. It is a lager-like ale strain that's lightly fruity, crisp and clean with a hint of sulfur that disappears with age to leave a clean ale. Accentuates hop flavors.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Lactobacillus Blend
yeasts.notes: A Lactobacillus brevis and plantarum blend with a wide temperature range. The Lacto plantarum, isolated in collaboration with Marz Community Brewing, sours efficiently at its higher end. Do not sour above 95°F to prevent stalling. Max souring develops within 24-48 hrs. Extremely hop sensitive, even 2 IBUs can prevent souring.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Lager I
yeasts.notes: Early inspiration for light American lager and thought to be from Budejovice, this crisp, balanced strain is lightly malty and finishes with very slight fruit notes. It is the backbone of the classic Czech Pilsner profile where the yeast character should neither dominate nor disappear among the beer's subtle balance of malts and hops.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: London Ale
yeasts.notes: The London Ale strain is a high attenuator that has obvious English character in its pronounced mineral and mild fruit. It performs best for dry, crisp beers, and in highlighting hop bitterness. For more neutral strains, try West Coast Ale I (OYL-004), or keep the English deportment with British Ale I (OYL-006) or British Ale VI (OYL-013).
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Lutra Kveik
yeasts.best_for: Kveik, American IPA, Hazy IPA, American Pale Ale, Black IPA, Red IPA, Red Ale, Robust Porter, American Stout, Winter Seasonal Beer, English IPA, Extra Special Bitter, Bitter, Stout, Tropical, Blonde Ale, American Strong Ale, Cream Ale, American Amber Lager, American Brown Ale, White IPA & Imperial IPA
yeasts.notes: Isolated from our Hornindal Kveik (OYL-091) culture, Lutra is shockingly clean with unrivaled speed when pitched at 90°F (32°C). The strain is perfect for brewing a refreshing pseudo-lager without the lead time of a lager. Lutra is your worry-free way to navigate the evolving demand for cold ones.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Mexican Lager
yeasts.notes: This great lager strain is thought to originate from a well known Mexican brewery. Simply put, it is clean, crisp, bright and versatile.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: New Jersey Ale
yeasts.notes: The New Jersey Ale (OYL-045) from Omega Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast that is highly flocculent and has an attenuation of 76.0%. It is designed to ferment at temperatures between 19.0-22.0 °C with a high alcohol tolerance, making it ideal for creating robust yet balanced ales. With its clean flavor profile and higher fermentation temperature, it's perfect for producing English style ales and American Pale Ales .
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Northwest Farmhouse Brett
yeasts.notes: Enjoy the lighter side of funkiness with this B. bruxellensis variant that hails from a Northwest U.S. brewery. It's known for its wonderful white wine character and light funk, and develops its character rather quickly. Brett character will be apparent within a few weeks of reaching terminal gravity and will continue to develop if given additional conditioning time.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Oktoberfest
yeasts.notes: This strain is a slow fermenter but said to be worth the wait by fans of Märzenbier and Oktoberfest Lagers particularly. It facilitates a smooth, rich, balanced beer with full, malty profile. Make sure to give it a thorough diacetyl rest.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Pacific NW Ale
yeasts.notes: A strain from the Pacific NW, originally from the UK, the Pacific NW Ale strain presents a relatively neutral profile with notes of malt and light fruit that add depth of flavor. It is a healthy flocculator.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Pediococcus
yeasts.notes: This modestly hop tolerant Pedio strain produces a clean lactic tang over time. The strain can produce diacetyl so it is often paired with one or more Brett strains (to consume the diacetyl). While more hop tolerant than the Lacto Blend (OYL-605), IBUs over 5-10 IBU may inhibit souring. Souring time can vary depending on IBU level.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Pilsner I
yeasts.notes: Thought to be the H strain of the famous Plzen brewer, this lager strain has a dry and neutral taste profile and is gently malty with a lightly perceptible floral aroma. The first of the famous Czech strains inspiring America's most famous light, brilliantly clear, golden lagers. Commonly produces sulfur during fermentation that clears during lagering. Watch out for diacetyl.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Pilsner II
yeasts.notes: Thought to be the D strain of the famous Pilsen brewer. With a dry and malty taste profile, it is the second of the famous Czech strains inspiring America's most famous light, brilliantly clear, golden lagers.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Saisonstein's Monster
yeasts.notes: An Omega-original, genetic hybrid of two Saison strains (French (OYL-026) and Belgian I (OYL-027)), Saisonstein's Monster is versatile, aromatic and attenuative with a silky mouthfeel. Excels in high gravity, ferments more reliably and thoroughly than its parents, and is spicy, complex, tart, dry and crisp. Some bubblegum from the Belgian, more fruit and fewer phenolics than the French.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Scottish Ale
yeasts.notes: The Scottish Ale strain is a flocculent, versatile and reliable house strain that produces neutral to complex and malty profiles in its fairly wide temperature range. Hop character is not muted by this strain. More esters emerge at higher fermentation temperatures.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Sundew Ale
yeasts.notes: Omega Yeast Labs' Sundew Ale (OYL-401) is a liquid ale yeast that is highly flocculent and offers an attenuation of 78.0%. It has a high alcohol tolerance of up to 12%, and performs best at a fermentation temperature between 18.0-26.0 °C. This versatile yeast is suitable for the production of a wide range of ales, such as English IPAs, Red Ales, and Brown Ales .
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Tropical IPA
yeasts.notes: A unique Saccharomyces strain that produces delicate, tart, tropical mango and pineapple fruit characteristics with a clean finish. Try higher fermentation temperatures to really bring out the tropical aspects. It's stubbornly nonflocculent, but the results are worth the trouble.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Voss Kveik
yeasts.best_for: Kveik, American IPA, Hazy IPA, American Pale Ale, Black IPA, Red IPA, Red Ale, Robust Porter, American Stout, Winter Seasonal Beer, English IPA, Extra Special Bitter, Bitter, Stout, Tropical, Blonde Ale, American Strong Ale, Cream Ale, American Amber Lager, American Brown Ale, White IPA & Imperial IPA
yeasts.notes: A traditional Norwegian kveik directly from the Gjernes farmstead, Voss Kveik's orange-citrus notes present throughout its wide temperature range. So, like the mango-honey profile of Hothead (OYL-057), Voss Kveik's orange-citrus is relatively clean across its fermentation temperature range, and pairs well with citrusy, fruity hops. Ester intensity and fermentation speed take off at higher temperatures. Non-phenolic and no fusels, even at higher temperatures.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: West Coast Ale I
yeasts.notes: Chico is a reliable, versatile and popular neutral foundation for displays of malts and hops. Highly attenuating and moderately flocculating, it ferments crisp and clean with light citrus notes under 66.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: West Coast Ale II
yeasts.notes: West Coast Ale II is a consistent, well flocculating, well attenuating and easy clearing neutral strain. Slightly fruitier than West Coast Ale I (OYL-004) and clean with a lightly perceptible nuttiness, its subtle citrus character finishes slightly tart at the cool end, and more fruit character emerges as fermentation temperatures increase.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: West Coast Ale III
yeasts.notes: Neutral and versatile, this strain is low ester-producing with balanced flavor and aroma. Highly alcohol tolerant. Similar to West Coast Ale I (OYL-004) but faster and more flocculent.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: West Coast Ale IV
yeasts.notes: An easy to handle strain, this neutral-tasting, quick-and-good flocculator and highly productive top cropper has excellent attenuation. Any fruity esters are somewhat mild through its higher temperature range, though they do decrease at the lower end. The relatively subtle yeast-contributed flavor cedes pleasantly to hops and malts.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: West Coast Lager
yeasts.notes: A lager strain that performs very well at ale temperatures, this strain is ideal for California common beer, also known as steam beer. Malty and crystal clear, it is considered by many to be best in its upper temperature range, around 65°F / 18°C.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Wit
yeasts.notes: Enthusiastically top cropping, this essential Wit yeast is distinctive for the popular, refreshing, easy-drinking summer style. Spicy phenolics carry the flavoring, while at the same time being supported—but not overshadowed— by good ester character. Lightly tart and dry
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: American Lager RVA
yeasts.notes: The American Lager (RVA 301) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid lager yeast strain that offers great flocculation and attenuation. With an attenuation of 77.5%, medium flocculation and alcohol tolerance, this yeast is ideal for making a range of lager beers. The optimal fermentation temperature for this strain is between 10-13 °C for the best results. This yeast can also be used to produce a wide variety of other beer styles including ales, pilsners, and wheat beers.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Belgian 1833 Ale RVA
yeasts.notes: The Belgian 1833 Ale (RVA 221) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast with a medium flocculation and attenuation of 76.5%. It has a medium alcohol tolerance and ferments best at temperatures between 19.0-21.0 °C. This yeast is perfect for producing Belgian ales, with their characteristic light fruitiness, subtle spiciness, and slight tartness. It adds complexity to beers that are dry, smooth and full-bodied, making it an excellent choice for brewers looking to create an authentic Belgian beer experience.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Boston Ale RVA
yeasts.notes: The Boston Ale (RVA 102) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast perfect for creating a wide range of full-bodied ales. It has an attenuation of 72.5% and medium flocculation, making it suitable for any style of ale. With its high alcohol tolerance, this strain can tolerate up to 12% ABV and beyond. The optimal fermentation temperature is 18.0-23.0 °C, making it suitable for most brewing conditions. This yeast produces a noticeable but not overpowering ester profile that adds complexity to the finished product.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Chico Ale
yeasts.notes: This versatile workhorse yeast will produce a clean crisp flavor profile with muted yeast character allowing hops and malt to take center stage. The American IPA has gained international acclaim and this is the yeast that did it.
yeasts.source_names: BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Chico Ale RVA
yeasts.notes: The Chico Ale (RVA 101) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast that is perfect for making American style ales. It has an attenuation of 77.5%, a medium flocculation rate, and a high alcohol tolerance. This yeast is best used when fermentation temperatures are kept between 19.0-23.0 °C for optimal results. It will give your beer a dry finish with subtle fruity esters and low diacetyl character. Whether you're brewing a pale ale, IPA, or other American style beer, the Chico Ale (RVA 101) from RVA Yeast Labs will provide excellent fermentation activity and help you create the perfect beer.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Chiswick Ale
yeasts.notes: This classic English strain from Fuller's Brewery will produce a very clear beer with some residual sweetness.
yeasts.source_names: BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Chiswick Ale RVA
yeasts.notes: The Chiswick Ale (RVA 131) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast perfect for producing classic English-style ales. It is characterized by very high flocculation and an attenuation of 68.5%, meaning it produces a beer with good body, not overly dry. Its alcohol tolerance is medium, so it can handle up to around 6-7% ABV without issue. The ideal fermentation temperature for this yeast is 18.0-21.0 °C, making it suitable for a wide range of temperatures.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Czech Lager RVA
yeasts.notes: RVA Yeast Labs' Czech Lager (RVA 304) is a liquid lager yeast that produces a clean, crisp beer with medium flocculation and attenuation of 77.5%. It has a medium alcohol tolerance and is best used at temperatures between 10.0 to 13.0 °C for optimal performance. This strain is perfect for producing classic lagers like Pilsner, Oktoberfest, Marzen and Vienna lagers, as well as many other styles like American Amber Lagers or California Common beers.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Dublin Ale RVA
yeasts.notes: The Dublin Ale (RVA 151) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast that is ideal for creating high-alcohol ales. It has a medium-high flocculation and an attenuation of 72.5%. This yeast can tolerate alcohol concentrations up to 12% ABV and should be fermented between 18.0-21.0 °C for best results. It produces a clean, neutral flavor profile with subtle notes of fruitiness, making it the perfect choice for brewers looking to create complex beers with big flavors and higher alcohol content.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: German Ale I RVA
yeasts.notes: German Ale I (RVA 161) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast that offers brewers a broad fermentation temperature range of 16.0-20.0 °C. This versatile yeast has a medium flocculation level and attenuation of 73.0%, providing brewers with good clarity in the finished beer. It also has a medium alcohol tolerance, making it an ideal choice for creating traditional German ales such as Kölsch and Altbier .
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Ghost Ale RVA
yeasts.notes: The Ghost Ale (RVA 263) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast with medium attenuation, medium flocculation and medium alcohol tolerance. It's ideal fermentation temperature range is 18.0-27.0 °C and it produces a slightly estery flavor profile. This versatile yeast can be used for a wide range of styles including American Pale Ales, Blonde Ales, Porters and Stouts. The Ghost Ale (RVA 263) imparts a fruity flavor with notes of citrus, apple and pear. It also has low sulfur production and is capable of fermenting in temperatures up to 27°C. All these properties make the Ghost Ale (RVA 263) an excellent choice for brewing balanced beers with complexity and character.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Golden Strong Ale RVA
yeasts.notes: RVA Yeast Labs' Golden Strong Ale (RVA 251) is a liquid ale yeast perfect for creating stronger, maltier beers. It offers a high degree of attenuation at 76.5%, meaning that it will convert a lot of the sugars in the beer into alcohol, leading to a higher ABV. The flocculation of this yeast is medium, so it should form a good amount of sediment in the bottom of your fermenter. With an alcohol tolerance of up to 12%, this yeast can handle strong beers without any problems. Lastly, it works best when fermented between 20 and 24 degrees Celsius.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Hoptopper Ale
yeasts.best_for: IPA, Double IPA, Pale Ale, Bitters
yeasts.notes: Isolated from a very well regarded example of a Double IPA, this strain will produce fruity esters which serve well to complement a heavy hop load. Great for a variety of pale ales and bitters.
yeasts.source_names: BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Hoptopper Ale RVA
yeasts.notes: Hoptopper Ale (RVA 104) by RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast designed to produce a full bodied, clean tasting beer with a crisp finish. This strain of yeast has good attenuation at 77.5%, medium-low flocculation, and can tolerate high levels of alcohol. It works best when fermented at temperatures ranging from 18.0-24.0 °C, allowing for a wide range of flavor profiles depending on the environment it is brewed in. Hoptopper Ale (RVA 104) creates smooth and well balanced beers that are sure to be crowd pleasers.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Manchester Ale
yeasts.notes: Dryer than the Chiswick, this English classic will create a touch of esters and leave a hint of residual sweetness and malt backbone.
yeasts.source_names: BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Manchester Ale RVA
yeasts.notes: Manchester Ale (RVA 132) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast that is well suited for a variety of ales. It has a high flocculation, meaning it will clump together and settle to the bottom of the fermenter quickly and easily. This strain has an attenuation of 72.5%, which produces a medium-bodied beer with a good balance between malt and hop flavors. Additionally, the alcohol tolerance of this strain is medium, so it can handle up to 8% ABV without any issues. The ideal fermentation temperature range for Manchester Ale (RVA 132) is 18-22°C, making it perfect for creating ales in almost any climate.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: München Lager RVA
yeasts.notes: München Lager (RVA 302) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid lager yeast with high flocculation and medium alcohol tolerance. It has an attenuation of 77.5%, meaning it can convert a significant amount of sugar into alcohol and carbon dioxide, making it ideal for lagers. The optimal fermentation temperature range for this yeast strain is 14.0-18.0 °C, making it suitable to brew in cooler temperatures that are typical of lagers.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Oktoberfest Lager
yeasts.notes: This is a bock-style lager yeast that accentuates maltiness.
yeasts.source_names: BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Oktoberfest Lager RVA
yeasts.notes: Oktoberfest Lager (RVA 303) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid lager yeast with medium flocculation and medium alcohol tolerance. It has an attenuation of 69.0% and should be fermented at temperatures between 11.0-14.0 °C for best results. This strain is perfect for creating deep, malty flavors while still having a crisp finish - ideal for German-style Oktoberfest beers!
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Pacman Ale
yeasts.best_for: Pale Ale, Blonde Ale, American Wheat, Altbier, Amber Ale
yeasts.notes: Originating from Rogue brewery in Newport, OR. Pacman is a very versatile yeast, and produces a dry, clean beer with little diacetyl and very mild esters.
yeasts.source_names: BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Pacman Ale RVA
yeasts.notes: The Pacman Ale (RVA 103) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast strain that offers high attenuation and medium-high flocculation. This strain has a high alcohol tolerance, making it an ideal choice for higher ABV beers. It ferments best between 17.0-22.0 °C, allowing brewers to craft ales with unique flavor profiles in a variety of temperature ranges. This strain is perfect for creating classic American-style ales with balanced bitterness and fruity esters.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Saison I RVA
yeasts.notes: Saison I (RVA 261) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast perfect for saisons and other Belgian-style ales. It has an attenuation of 70% and medium flocculation, making it ideal for producing a beer with high alcohol content and a dry finish. This yeast can tolerate medium levels of alcohol and prefers to ferment between 24.0-29.0°C for best results. It is known for its complex fruity aroma and flavour, with notes of pineapple, pear, lemon, and clove.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Saison II RVA
yeasts.notes: Saison II (RVA 262) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast strain that has an attenuation of 78.5%, medium flocculation, a medium alcohol tolerance, and its ideal fermentation temperature is 19.0-25.0 °C. This yeast strain produces beers with low ester production and high attenuation, making it perfect for producing Belgian-style Saisons, witbiers, and farmhouse ales. The aroma produced by this strain can be described as spicy and earthy, adding complexity to the finished beer. Saison II (RVA 262) can also be used as a base strain in wild fermentations due to its moderate alcohol tolerance and neutral flavor profile.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Scotch Ale RVA
yeasts.notes: The Scotch Ale (RVA 141) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast with medium flocculation and a high alcohol tolerance. It has an attenuation rate of 72.5% and an ideal fermentation temperature range of 18.0-21.0 °C, making it perfect for making deep, flavorful beers at home. Its clean flavor profile and wide temperature range make it great for brewing ales that are strong yet mellow with just the right amount of sweetness, providing craft beer enthusiasts with the perfect balance for their creations.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Trappist Ale I RVA
yeasts.notes: The Trappist Ale I (RVA 201) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast that produces a high alcohol tolerance of up to 12% ABV. It has a medium flocculation and an attenuation rate of 77.5%. The best fermentation temperature for this yeast strain is between 18-22°C, making it suitable for brewing traditional Belgian ales at home. This yeast strain boasts an array of complex and diverse flavors, offering unique depth and character to any beer brewed with it.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Trappist Ale II RVA
yeasts.notes: The Trappist Ale II (RVA 202) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast designed to ferment high alcohol beers. With an attenuation rating of 77.5%, this yeast allows for a wide range of beer styles to be crafted, ranging from light and crisp to full-bodied and complex. It has a medium flocculation rate, meaning it will settle well during fermentation, leaving behind minimal sediment. This yeast also features a high alcohol tolerance, allowing for higher ABV beers without risking off flavors or reduced attenuation. For best results, it is recommended that the fermentation occur between 18.0-22.0°C for optimal flavor development.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Trappist Ale III RVA
yeasts.notes: The Trappist Ale III (RVA 203) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast. This yeast has an attenuation of 77.5%, and a medium flocculation rate, making it suitable for use in many types of beer recipes. Its high alcohol tolerance makes it a great choice for styles like Belgian Tripels, Belgian Dubbels, and other high gravity beers. The ideal fermentation temperature range is 18.0-22.0 °C, which makes it well suited to fermenting in most conditions without any significant issues.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Trappist Ale IV RVA
yeasts.notes: The Trappist Ale IV (RVA 204) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast with a high level of alcohol tolerance. It has a medium flocculation and an attenuation of 77.5%. This strain is ideal for fermenting at temperatures between 18 - 22°C, making it an excellent choice for those looking to craft delicious Belgian-style ales. Its high alcohol tolerance also makes it suitable for higher gravity beers that require extra fermentation time or have a longer maturation period.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Verboten Ale RVA
yeasts.notes: Verboten Ale (RVA 241) from RVA Yeast Labs is a liquid ale yeast designed for brewers looking to create a range of high-alcohol beers. With an attenuation of 72.5%, it provides a high amount of alcohol content in the finished product. It has low flocculation, meaning it will remain suspended in the beer rather than settle out at the bottom, adding more body and mouthfeel. Additionally, Verboten Ale has a high alcohol tolerance of up to 15% ABV, allowing brewers to craft drinks with an extra kick. This yeast ferments best between 18.0 and 24.0°C and is suitable for use in Belgian golden ales, English strong ales, British bitters, and more.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Lucky No. 7
yeasts.notes: Real Brewers Lucky No. 7 is a liquid ale yeast with high flocculation and an attenuation rate of 75%. It has an alcohol tolerance of up to 10% and ferments best at temperatures between 20-24°C. This yeast strain produces a full bodied beer with subtle esters, allowing for a variety of brewing styles including ales, lagers, stouts, and wheat beers. The resultant beers are known for their complexity, flavor depth, and drinkability.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: The Monk
yeasts.notes: The Monk is a liquid ale yeast from Real Brewers, offering a medium flocculation and an attenuation of 78.0%. It has an alcohol tolerance of up to 15.0%, and performs best when fermented at temperatures between 19.0-22.0 °C. This yeast can produce high levels of esters and phenolic compounds, making it ideal for producing Belgian-style ales with complex flavor profiles such as Witbiers, Farmhouse Ales, Saisons, Dubbels, Tripels or Belgian Strong Ales .
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: The One
yeasts.notes: The One from Real Brewers is a liquid ale yeast with high flocculation and an attenuation of 75.0%. This robust yeast is well-suited for a variety of ales, and it is best used in environments between 20.0-24.0 °C for optimal fermentation. It is known for being reliable and consistent in its performance, making it the perfect choice for any brewer looking to create delicious ales without worry or hassle.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Ye Olde English
yeasts.notes: Ye Olde English is a liquid ale yeast produced by Real Brewers, with an attenuation rate of 70.0%. With a medium flocculation rate, this yeast is perfect for achieving a full-bodied flavor in your beer. The ideal fermentation temperature range for this strain is between 18.0 and 21.0°C, allowing brewers to create a unique flavor experience without worrying about extreme temperatures.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: DADY
yeasts.notes: The " DADY " of Red Star is a dry ale yeast with low flocculation and high alcohol tolerance. It has an attenuation of 65.0%, meaning that it will convert most of the available sugars into alcohol. The ideal fermentation temperature for this yeast is between 18.0-27.0 °C, making it suitable for a wide variety of styles, from light ales to heavier Belgian and dark ales. This yeast strain is known for producing full-bodied beers with complex flavors and aromas, and its high alcohol tolerance makes it perfect for strong beer styles such as barley wines.

yeasts.name: Premier Blanc
yeasts.notes: The Premier Blanc (UCD595) of Red Star is a dry wine and cider yeast that has low flocculation. It is highly alcohol tolerant with an ideal fermentation temperature between 15.0-30.0 °C, making it very versatile and suitable for a variety of fermentations. This makes it perfect for use in both red and white wines as well as ciders, giving lots of different possibilities to explore aromas, flavours, and textures.

yeasts.name: Alt Ale BRY
yeasts.notes: Alt Ale (BRY 144) is a liquid ale yeast produced by Siebel Institute. This strain has an attenuation of 78.0%, which allows brewers to achieve a balanced malt profile and full, rounded body. The flocculation of this yeast is medium, ensuring that fermentation will be complete in the desired timeframe. For optimal performance, it is recommended to ferment at a temperature between 15.0-20.0 °C for the best flavor and aroma profiles. Alt Ale (BRY 144) is suitable for many styles of beer including Altbier, Kölsch, Dortmunder Export, and more!
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: American Ale BRY
yeasts.notes: The American Ale (BRY 96) is a liquid ale yeast manufactured by the Siebel Institute. This type of yeast has a medium flocculation rate and an attenuation of 78.0%. It is best used at fermentation temperatures between 18.0-22.0°C for optimal performance and flavor profile. The American Ale (BRY 96) is great for making full-bodied ales with a slightly fruity taste, and can be used in many different beer styles such as pale ales, IPAs, stouts, and lagers.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: American Lager BRY
yeasts.notes: The American Lager (BRY 118) yeast from the Siebel Institute is a liquid lager yeast. It has a high flocculation, meaning it will settle quickly at the bottom of the fermenter. This particular strain is highly attenuative and can ferment up to 72%. The ideal fermentation temperature for this strain is between 20 to 22°C. This lager yeast produces a clean and crisp flavor profile with slight malt character, making it ideal for light lagers like Budweiser or Coors.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Bavarian Weizen Ale BRY
yeasts.notes: The Bavarian Weizen Ale (BRY 235) from the Siebel Institute is a liquid ale yeast strain with a high flocculation profile and an attenuation of 73.0%. It is ideal for brewing light wheat beers, with the optimal fermentation temperature at 10.0-14.0°C. The strain provides a subtle fruitiness and flavor complexity, while also producing classic phenols, esters, and banana notes that are characteristic of Bavarian wheat beers. It has good sedimentation qualities, resulting in clear, bright beers with low haze levels. BRY 235 is an excellent choice for traditional Bavarian wheat beer styles such as Hefeweizen or Kristalweizen.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: English Ale BRY
yeasts.notes: English Ale (BRY 264) is an ale yeast from the Siebel Institute. It is a liquid form of yeast with medium flocculation and an attenuation of 78.0%. The ideal fermentation temperature for this strain is 15.0-20.0 °C, making it perfect for producing classic English ales such as Pale Ales, Bitters, Milds and Stouts. This yeast strain produces a smooth, well balanced flavor profile with subtle fruity esters and low levels of diacetyl.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: German Kölsch BRY
yeasts.notes: The German Kölsch (BRY 401) from Siebel Institute is a liquid ale yeast that produces a crisp, slightly fruity beer. This yeast has an attenuation of 72.0% and flocculation of low, meaning it will ferment quickly and the resulting beer will be highly carbonated with good clarity. Ideal fermentation temperatures for this strain are 13.0-15.0 °C, so it should be fermented in cooler conditions for maximum flavor development. The end result will be a light, refreshing beer with subtle fruit notes and plenty of effervescence.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: North European Lager BRY
yeasts.notes: The North European Lager (BRY 203) from Siebel Institute is a liquid lager yeast with low flocculation. It has an attenuation of 78.0% and ferments best at temperatures of between 20.0-22.0 °C. It is well suited for German style lagers and pilsners, and can also be used to make crisp, dry beers with high drinkability. The BRY 203 produces a clean and clear beer without too much fruity or estery flavors, allowing the malt characters to shine through.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

yeasts.name: Trappist Ale BRY
yeasts.notes: The Trappist Ale (BRY 204) yeast strain from the Siebel Institute is a liquid form ale yeast with a medium flocculation and high attenuation of 78.0%. This strain is well suited to creating classic Belgian-style ales and produces a complex, spicy flavour profile. This unique yeast strain works best at temperatures between 18.0-22.0 °C for optimal fermentation and flavor development. It is an excellent choice for producing Abbey Ales, Dubbels, Tripels, Quads, Saisons, and other special Belgian ales that require fruity esters and phenolics to achieve their distinct character.
yeasts.source_names: beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005

Together these strains produce a dry beer with a vinous quality and a flavor profile of dried dark fruit, plum, leather, and a mild earthy funk and acidity. Both strains in this blend are very alcohol tolerant (10-15%). While this blend is fairly versatile, its complexity truly shines in dark beers.

yeasts.name: Dry Belgian Ale
yeasts.notes: The Yeast Bay's Dry Belgian Ale (WLP4025) is a liquid ale yeast perfect for high gravity beers that require a dry finish. This yeast has a very high attenuation of 92.5%, which makes it ideal for producing dryer styles like tripels and dubbels. It also flocculates quite highly, providing the beer with clarity and body. WLP4025 has an alcohol tolerance of up to 12% ABV, and ferments best between 20-23°C. With this yeast you can easily craft a complex Belgian-style beer with extraordinary depth and flavor!

yeasts.name: Farmhouse Sour Ale
yeasts.notes: This blend contains two farmhouse STA1+ Saccharomyces cerevisiae isolates, Lactobacillus brevis, and Lactobacillus delbrueckii. The two Saccharomyces strains will combine to create a delightful ester profile of grapefruit and orange zest accompanied by a mild earthiness and spiciness, while the Lactobacillus strains will produce a balanced acid profile. This blend exhibits high diastatic activity.

yeasts.name: Flanders Specialty Ale

yeasts.notes: Flanders Specialty Ale is a single strain of Saccharomyces cerevisiae isolated from a fascinating Belgian producer of a wide array of traditional Belgian beer styles. This is a versatile yeast that will ferment fairly dry and produce a balanced flavor and aroma profile laced with a myriad of esters and phenols.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

It exhibits a vibrant bouquet of hull melon and cantaloupe esters across a broad temperature range. This strain is well suited to any hop forward or farmhouse-inspired beers.

yeasts.name: Franconian Dark Lager
yeasts.notes: Franconian Dark Lager is a single strain of Saccharomyces pastorianus that hails from the Franconia region of Germany. This yeast exhibits a short lag time and has flavor profile characteristics that complement dark, roasted malts. While the dark malt complementarity makes this yeast a perfect fit for any big malt driven dark lagers, it's also able to produce crisp light lagers.

yeasts.name: Funktown Pale Ale
yeasts.notes: Funktown Pale Ale is a blend of The Yeast Bay's Vermont Ale strain and a unique strain of STA1 + Saccharomyces cerevisiae that is well suited for primary fermentation. The combination of citrus, peach, pineapple and mango esters produce a unique flavor and aroma profile that is fruit-forward and complements any hop-forward beer. This blend exhibits low diastatic activity.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Hazy Daze
yeasts.notes: Hazy Daze contains a proprietary blend of three Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains, all of which offer unique contributions to the production of crisp, hop forward beers. Expect this blend to throw bountiful amounts of peach, apricot, nectarine and grapefruit citrus esters and achieve good attenuation.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Hazy Daze II
yeasts.notes: Hazy Daze II is a proprietary blend of three Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains and one STA1+ Saccharomyces cerevisiae strain. It will exhibit an strong ester profile of stone fruit (peach, apricot, nectarine and), tropical fruit (mango, guava) and grapefruit citrus esters. It ferments faster and finishes slightly drier compared to our Hazy Daze. This blend exhibits low diastatic activity.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Hessian Pils
yeasts.notes: Hessian Pils is a single strain of Saccharomyces pastorianus that hails from the Hess region of Germany. It exhibits everything you want in a great Pilsner yeast: it's a clean fermenter with low ester formation, exhibits a short lag time, ferments wort quickly and attenuates well even at the low end of the temperature range. These characteristics allow the malt and hop profile to really shine, and creates a crisp finished beer.
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Lactobacillus brevis - Strain TYB282

yeasts.notes: TYB282 is a single strain of Lactobacillus brevis isolated out of an unintentionally soured golden ale produced by a Mexican craft brewery. This strain produces a nice, clean lactic acidity (down to ~pH 3.16-3.18) in unhopped wort within 36 hours at a temperature of ~72-77 °F. The higher the temperature up to 90 °F, the faster the acid production. This is a great strain for kettle souring, but really shines in souring fermented beer as a result of its hop tolerance (15-20 IBU).

yeasts.name: Metschnikowia reukaufii
yeasts.best_for: The functional properties of brewing yeasts have a direct impact on the performance, quality and economics of the resulting beer.
yeasts.notes: M. reukaufii is a nectar specialist that was isolated from flowers in the Berkeley Hills of California. Evolutionarily, these yeast likely evolved to produce a more odorous and attractive nectar for pollinators by enzymatically altering otherwise inodorous nectar compounds like glycosides. While only attenuating to 20-25% in brewer’s wort and not utilizing maltose or maltose polymers, in co-fermentations it has been shown to drop gravity and pH of the fermentation faster, accentuate and modulate the flavor and aroma profile and soften the perceived bitterness of the finished product. This strain MUST be used in conjunction with other yeast that can ferment brewer’s wort (capable of fermenting maltose).
yeasts.source_names: Brewtarget DefaultContent004 (more yeasts); beer-analytics.com via Brewtarget DefaultContent005; BeerProto dataset

yeasts.name: Midwestern Ale

A relatively fast fermenter with good attenuation, expect this yeast to ferment cleaner with a low ester profile at the cooler fermentation temperatures, and produce a more pronounced ester profile at warmer fermentation temperatures. This yeast is a great choice for a versatile house yeast.

yeasts.name: Saison-Brett Blend

yeasts.name: Sake

yeasts.name: West Yorkshire Ale
